US Army to shut down unit in Europe focused on drone warfare in latest shakeup
A drone warfare US Army unit in Europe has been told to return to being a traditional infantry battalion.
For more nearly a year, soldiers of the 173rd Airborne Brigade have been experimenting and building their own drones, as well as participating in drills on waging unmanned warfare after Ukraine pioneered such tactics in its yearslong conflict with Russia.
In November, 600 soldiers formed a battalion that specialised in drone warfare and was set up to be used as a dedicated unit that could deploy anywhere drones were required.
Iranian oil offers to Chinese buyers fall as US blockade bites, sources say
Offers to Chinese buyers of Iranian crude have declined and prices have risen this week as a US blockade continues to cut off Tehran’s shipments and the threat of sanctions from Washington, trade sources told Reuters.
The number of offers for Iranian oil cargoes to China for September and October delivery has declined from July and August cargoes, four trade sources familiar with the matter said. The offers have declined as barrels already in ships on the water have been sold, they said.
The US reimposed its blockade of Iran’s shipping and ports on 13 July.
Tehran has condemned the threat of sanctions as “economic terrorism”.
summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that it is time to end the war with the US from a position of strength, while Tehran vowed a crushing response to new US threats of economic sanctions. Meanwhile, Gulf countries are making preparations to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, and the USS George Washington aircraft carrier arrived in the Middle East to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln. Additionally, a British teenager pleaded guilty to an arson attack on offices linked to the Iran International television station in London.
key_points: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian called for ending the war with the US while claiming Iran is in a position of power and dignity.
The US military reported 757 injuries and 18 deaths since the conflict began, while the USS George Washington arrived in the Middle East to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln.
Gulf countries like Dubai are exploring alternative trade routes and facilities to bypass the Strait of Hormuz amid ongoing disruptions.
A 19-year-old British man pleaded guilty to an arson attack on premises belonging to Volant Media, the parent company of Iran International.
Iran threatened a devastating response following US plans to impose severe new economic sanctions and maintain a naval blockade.

title: Pakistan’s ex-PM Imran Khan back in jail after brief hospital visit
author: Al Jazeera Staff
content:
![Security personnel cordon off a street outside the Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad on August 20, 2026 after Pakistan's Supreme Court ordered to transfer jailed former prime minister Imran Khan to hospital for medical treatment.](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/afp_6a87676218f1-1787258722.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
Pakistan’s former Prime Minister Imran Khan has been transferred back to prison after a brief stay at a hospital in the capital, Islamabad.
Khan, 73, was moved from Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail to the state-run PIMS Hospital early on Friday, where doctors conducted a medical checkup amid long-running concerns over his health.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items
- list 1 of 4Pakistan challenges top court order to move Imran Khan to private hospital
- list 2 of 4Pakistan top court orders Imran Khan’s hospital transfer amid access battle
- list 3 of 4Pakistan’s Khan in jail for 3 years: PTI rallies over ‘arbitrary detention’
- list 4 of 4Clashes on anniversary of Imran Khan imprisonment
The founder of the opposition Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party had been expected to undergo the examination at the privately run Shifa International Hospital, but was taken to PIMS due to a “security situation created by PTI workers,” according to Information Minister Attaullah Tarar.
Earlier, security had been tightened around Shifa ahead of Khan’s expected arrival. A senior official said that hundreds of police and paramilitary personnel had been deployed in the area.
The minister confirmed that Khan was taken to the hospital during the night, where a specialised medical team, including a cardiologist, an ophthalmologist and a physician, examined the former prime minister and “declared him medically fit”. Tarar added that Khan’s sister, Uzma Khan, was present during the entire visit.
The hospital visit followed a Supreme Court order on Tuesday directing authorities to move the imprisoned former leader to hospital within two days. The court said an independent medical board should assess Khan’s condition and include his personal physician.
The court order followed a report submitted to the court on Monday by Adiala jail’s superintendent, detailing an August 10 assessment by a cardiac board. The report recorded fluctuating blood pressure and anxiety that it said was linked to contact with Khan’s family being restricted.
The government had challenged the order, but officials said preparations for Khan’s transfer were completed on Thursday.
Khan’s family and his party have repeatedly appealed to the courts over his health during the past year, particularly concerns about the vision in his right eye.
Courts have twice declined similar requests to move Khan to hospital since February. In one case, the Islamabad High Court instead ordered an assessment by a medical board.
Khan lost power in April 2022 after losing a no-confidence motion in the parliament. He has been in prison since August 2023, when a court convicted him in a case involving the sale of state gifts, charges which he has consistently denied.
The former cricket star and his wife Bushra Bibi have since been convicted in several other cases and have denied all wrongdoing, saying the prosecutions are politically motivated.
summary: Pakistan's former Prime Minister Imran Khan was transferred back to prison following a brief medical checkup at a state-run hospital in Islamabad. The Supreme Court had previously ordered authorities to move the 73-year-old jailed leader for an evaluation amid ongoing health concerns raised by his family and party. A specialized medical team examined Khan and declared him medically fit before he was returned to jail.
key_points: Imran Khan was temporarily moved from Adiala jail to the state-run PIMS Hospital following a Supreme Court order.
A specialized medical team, including a cardiologist, ophthalmologist, and physician, examined Khan and declared him medically fit.
Khan was initially slated for a private hospital, but security concerns raised by PTI workers led to his transfer to PIMS instead.
Khan has been imprisoned since August 2023 and faces multiple convictions, which he and his party maintain are politically motivated.

title: Australian hiker's body recovered as police probe error reporting she was alive
author: Harry Sekulich
content:
![Chris Minns speaks at a press conference, wearing a navy jacket and blue collared shirt. He has brown hair with grey tips.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/0161/live/bfab9ab0-9d13-11f1-aa70-15b2bc2a2471.jpg)
NSW premier Chris Minns apologised to Lily Hooper's family after she was wrongly identified as alive
- Published
The body of missing Australian hiker Lily Hooper has been recovered as officials investigate a "miscommunication" that briefly reported she had been found alive.
Within minutes of reports first emerging that she was alive on Thursday, police confirmed that Hooper had been found deceased in the bushland of the Southern Highlands in New South Wales (NSW).
State premier Chris Minns and NSW police commissioner Mal Lanyon apologised to her family on Friday over the error.
Hooper, 18, an experienced hiker, was reported missing last week triggering an eight-day search which involved approximately 1,000 people.
![A blonde woman in a green singlet is pictured in the left. On the right, the same woman is seen sitting on a plane, with her hair in two plaits.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/c439/live/7851db30-9c3b-11f1-853e-ad17ff71705c.jpg)
Lily Hooper, 18, was found dead after an eight-day search in the Australian bush
A police spokesperson confirmed to BBC News on Friday that her body had been airlifted from the Nattai National Park, south-west of Sydney.
"A post-mortem examination will be conducted in coming days to formally confirm ID and determine cause of death," the statement said.
Minns had told a state parliamentary hearing on Thursday that crews had found Hooper alive "with half a bottle of water" eight days after she was reported missing. Within 30 minutes, he corrected himself saying "Lily's body has been found" and she was deceased.
Media outlets in Australia widely reported the initial incorrect reports that Hooper was located alive before retracting their stories shortly after.
The miscommunication meant there was a brief window in which her parents believed she was alive.
Speaking on Friday, Minns said he planned to speak directly to Hooper's family to issue a personal apology.
"The government, myself â we're profoundly sorry", he said.
NSW State Emergency Services commissioner Mike Wassing said that codes are often assigned during major searches.
Such terms can avoid sensitive details being shared over radio broadcasts during a search, when friends, relatives and community volunteers are usually involved alongside emergency service personnel and police officers.
"The codes are usually associated with some aspect like that in terms of bottles of water," Wassing told the Australian Broadcasting Corporation, although he did not confirm the cause of the error which is under investigation.
Lanyon said communications can be challenging during large searches in remote locations.
"Tragically, her condition was miscommunicated, and for that I apologise," he said.
Police will review policy and processes to ensure protocols are "foolproof" into the future, Lanyon added.
![Map of the Sydney region in New South Wales, Australia, showing the location of Nattai National Park. The park is highlighted with a red outline south-west of Sydney and north-west of Wollongong. Labels mark Sydney and Wollongong, while an inset map of Australia highlights the park's location in south-eastern Australia.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/71ff/live/e9348430-9cb6-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.png)
Hooper had been found in the southern highlands, a vast bushland area south-west of Sydney
summary: The body of 18-year-old missing Australian hiker Lily Hooper has been recovered from the bushland of New South Wales following an eight-day search. Officials are investigating a miscommunication after state premier Chris Minns wrongly announced during a parliamentary hearing that she had been found alive. Both Premier Minns and NSW police commissioner Mal Lanyon issued apologies to Hooper's family for the error, which caused them to briefly believe she was alive.
key_points: Lily Hooper, an 18-year-old experienced hiker, was found deceased in the Southern Highlands after an eight-day search involving about 1,000 people.
NSW Premier Chris Minns incorrectly stated at a parliamentary hearing that Hooper was found alive before correcting the statement within 30 minutes to confirm she was deceased.
Premier Chris Minns and NSW Police Commissioner Mal Lanyon apologized to Hooper's family for the miscommunication.
Police are investigating the cause of the reporting error and will review search policies and communication protocols.

title: Lily Hooper’s family was told she’d been found alive. ‘She’s coming home,’ her father said – then tears of joy turned to grief
author: Ima Caldwell
content:
The rugged landscape of the New South Wales southern highlands loomed large on Thursday evening. This country had just revived, then killed hope. A young woman was found “alive”, but then it was confirmed she was dead: desperation, confusion, tragedy reigned.
Here, where the bitumen of Wombeyan Caves Road runs into unsealed dirt, rolling hills dotted with cattle give way to expansive mountains. The late-afternoon sun sends long, beaming rays past the edges of clouds, casting a warm glow on distant cliff faces.
A few hours earlier, after eight agonising days of searchers scouring the Nattai national park, 90km south-west of Sydney, for the missing 18-year-old hiker Lily Hooper, fears had abruptly turned to joy. Police told her family she had been found alive.
Footage from Channel Seven showed the relief and elation. Family and friends embraced, in tears. Her father, Jim Hooper, said “they’re going to get her now by the sound of it … she might be going straight to hospital I’d say”.
He showed off the guitar and packet of Tim Tams he’d brought to the site “because it might lure her out of the bush”.
Her smiling mother, Kirrily, said she had washed her hair and “put my good sneakers on” in anticipation of good news.
There was a toast in celebration.
“I was never going to give up,” Jim said. “She’s a beautiful girl and she’s coming home.”
![The mountains where Lily Hooper went missing.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/ee61722d77d37836a360db0de9f07c4e43dcd8de/0_1476_3024_2419/master/3024.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
The NSW premier, Chris Minns, interrupted a grilling in an estimates hearing back in Sydney to announce the discovery about midday, sharing a curious detail that Lily had been found “with half a bottle of water”.
Hope was shattered barely 30 minutes later.
Minns, who had believed he was sharing good news, now interrupted proceedings again.
“I’ve got some terrible news,” he said. “I apologise … Lily’s body has been found.” The bottle of water reference may have been rescuer code – not proof of life.
The SES commissioner, Mick Wassing, on Friday would explain “it’s very common that code words are given to search and rescue crews” to avoid details being overheard by others on radios.
“My understanding is that that’s what has occurred in this situation,” Wassing said.
![The bitumen of Wombeyan Caves Road runs into the unsealed dirt of Wanganderry Road.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/a01f42dadf51b049ea3bdb9277adb5664d0e2ba8/0_0_3780_3024/master/3780.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
On Thursday in the mountains, TV cameras at the site backed away, showing the family embracing, now in grief.
The police commissioner, Mal Lanyon, later told reporters in Goulburn that the devastating miscommunication was “born out of elation”.
“Tragically, that miscommunication then led to a deflation, and obviously, we know now, an impact on her family,” Lanyon said.
Lily, an experienced hiker, had been found dead off the trail, a “significant distance” from her car.
The assistant commissioner Joseph Cassar told reporters in Moss Vale on Thursday afternoon that the searchers had carried handheld radios and faced communication challenges in the “thick, dense terrain”.
Nightfall
As the sun set over the southern highlands command post, the temperature dipped to a bitter chill. By 5.30pm, the sun was gone and the landscape stripped of its warmth, leaving muted greys and browns.
Police said Lily was last seen wearing a T-shirt and shorts, and it was unknown if she had any equipment with her.
The command post, where the search was coordinated, was now still. About 100 Australian Defence Force personnel had joined the operation in the 24 hours before the teenager was located. Almost 1,000 searchers and volunteers had been involved overall.
Emergency workers and volunteers were packing up and driving out on Thursday evening. A NSW Rural Fire Service vehicle slowly towed a trailer back down the dirt road, leaving the command post and passing police cars.
The mourning quiet was broken intermittently by the evening calls of birds and the low hum of idling engines.
A significant presence remained stationed at the operation base. Unmarked four-wheel drives sat alongside SES vehicles, police search and rescue vans, and a large police incident response unit.
The procedures of death were under way. In the distance, a group of officers wearing white jumpsuits gathered.
Hooper’s car had been parked near the trail head on Wanganderry Road at High Range, Cassar said.
The assistant commissioner said it was not yet clear how she died or if she had sustained injuries.
A report was to be prepared for the coroner, investigating the time, place and circumstances of Hooper’s death, in addition to the communications problems.
![A solitary helicopter sits near the dwindling, demobilised search party.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/35c8fd4c4e83a33fb100f2292489ddf84dcdc558/393_1001_3142_1892/master/3142.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
As night closed in, a solitary helicopter sat grounded in a field of tall, brown grass, near the demobilised search party. The last traces of light vanished entirely from the sky.
Then, the whir of a second helicopter overhead broke the silence, touching down at the command post, just as the landscape went dark.
On Friday morning, police announced that Hooper’s body had been winched out of the bush overnight.
summary: Following an eight-day search in the New South Wales southern highlands for missing 18-year-old hiker Lily Hooper, police initially informed her family that she had been found alive. Joy among family members and announcements from public officials quickly turned to grief roughly 30 minutes later when it was confirmed that her body had been found. Authorities attributed the false report to a miscommunication born from elation and potential search-and-rescue code words used over radios in dense terrain.
key_points: Eighteen-year-old hiker Lily Hooper went missing in the Nattai national park for eight days before being found dead.
Police initially told her family she was found alive, prompting public celebrations and joyful statements from her parents.
Roughly 30 minutes later, officials corrected the report, confirming that her body had been located.
Authorities blamed the tragic confusion on a miscommunication and possible rescue code words.
Police stated that a report would be prepared for the coroner regarding the circumstances of her death and the communication issues.

title: UK clashes with Israel over controversial West Bank settlement
author: Kate Devlin
content:
The UK has clashed with Israel over a controversial settlement project in the occupied West Bank.
Ed Miliband , the foreign secretary, called the country’s move to seek bidders to build 1,200 homes as part of the E1 settlement project an “unacceptable and destructive act”. He said the UK would not “stand back and accept the destruction of the two-state solution”.
Israel’s foreign minister, Gideon Sa’ar, hit back, accusing the UK of a “patronising tone” and an “absurd” stance.
Mr Miliband said the UK’s opposition to the E1 settlement project, which he said puts the two-state solution at risk by separating the West Bank from East Jerusalem, had been clear both in public and privately.
He said he had told Mr Sa’ar “that the Israeli government must halt E1 plans immediately, retract the tender and stop all settlement expansion”. The Foreign Office also summoned Israel’s chargé d’affaires, the country’s most senior diplomat, to set out the UK’s “profound objection to this move”.
Mr Miliband said the UK remained committed to supporting a two-state solution “as the only way to ensure long-term security and peace for both Palestinians and Israelis. All settlements damage that prospect and are a flagrant breach of international law.”
He added that in the coming weeks the UK would set out a series of measures “to respond to Israeli government policies, protect the viability of the Palestinian state, target sanctions at those who participate in illegal settlement expansion and support a just and lasting peace for Israelis and Palestinians”.
Mr Sa’ar accused Mr Miliband of being “entirely one-sided” and said he rejected his statement and “the patronising tone of his words”.
On X, formerly Twitter, he wrote: “It is absurd for Britain to lecture the Jewish people about where they may live in their historic tiny homeland, when the Jewish people’s connection and right to this land is the most extensively documented of any people in human history.
“There have been no new decisions regarding development in E1. The decision was made on 2025. The tender process has been under way for several months, with certain tender documents published only in recent days.”
Mr Sa’ar said the UK’s policy of “blaming only Israel while ignoring Palestinian extremism” had contributed to antisemitic hatred and attacks against the British Jewish community.
He added: “The UK government’s decision to damage the relationship between our countries is deeply unfortunate. But Israel will not be a passive victim of this policy. Israel will defend its rights, its interests and its people.”
Later on Thursday the UK, France, Germany and Italy issued a joint statement in which they urged Israel to “retract” its plans and warned businesses not to bid for construction tenders.
The statement warned: “International law is clear that Israeli settlements in the West Bank are illegal...At a time of grave instability in the West Bank with unprecedented levels of violence by settlers against civilians, and serious restrictions on the Palestinian economy, this decision is even more concerning.
“We urge the government of Israel to retract these plans immediately and end its expansion of settlements in the West Bank... businesses should not consider bidding for construction tenders. They should be aware of legal and reputational consequences including the risk of involving themselves in serious breaches of international law.”
summary: The UK and several European allies have clashed with Israel over a controversial West Bank settlement project to build 1,200 homes in the E1 area. UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband condemned the move as an unacceptable threat to the two-state solution and summoned Israel's chargé d'affaires. In response, Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar criticized the UK's stance as absurd and one-sided, while the UK, France, Germany, and Italy issued a joint statement urging Israel to retract the plans.
key_points: The UK condemned Israel's tender to build 1,200 homes in the E1 settlement project as a threat to the two-state solution.
The UK Foreign Office summoned Israel's chargé d'affaires to express profound objection and demanded the plans be halted.
Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar rejected the UK's criticism, accusing London of a patronizing tone and ignoring Palestinian extremism.
The UK, France, Germany, and Italy issued a joint statement urging Israel to retract the plans and warning businesses against bidding.

title: Five missing after fire in Alpine town in Switzerland
author: Ben Hatton
content:
![Large flames come out of the windows in the top floor of a building at night.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/b130/live/8dbc0170-9d27-11f1-889e-c901b814ac6c.jpg)
- Published
Five people are missing and eight others injured after a restaurant with apartments was "completely destroyed" by fire in the Swiss town of Thusis, police have said.
Initial investigations indicate the blaze broke out on the second floor and the cause was still being investigated, according to the GraubÃ¼nden cantonal police.
The force said it was called just after midnight local time (22:00 GMT on Thursday) and that nearly 100 firefighters responded. The roof had to be opened using a crane after the stairwell collapsed.
The Alpine GraubÃ¼nden region, also known as Grisons, is a popular holiday destination for both winter sports and summer nature activities in eastern Switzerland.
![The building as seen from the air - it is next to a river. Smoke rises from the building at night, while at least five fire engines are parked nearby and on the bridge over the river.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1200/cpsprodpb/6419/live/bfd92340-9d27-11f1-ba3e-c323fd3033f4.jpg)
Fourteen people escaped the building, police said, of whom two were seriously injured, two suffered moderate injuries and four suffered minor injuries.
People were taken to hospitals in Chur, Thusis, Ilanz, and Zurich, it added.
Police and the public prosecutor's office are investigating the cause of the fire.
![The building as seen from a bridge crossing a river. Three streams of water from firefighting crews douse the building. Smoke rises from the building - at night.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1200/cpsprodpb/c124/live/fe63e140-9d27-11f1-ba3e-c323fd3033f4.jpg)
summary: Five people are missing and eight others are injured after a fire completely destroyed a building containing a restaurant and apartments in Thusis, Switzerland. Police and firefighters responded to the blaze just after midnight, with nearly 100 firefighters tackling the flames. Fourteen people managed to escape the building, and an investigation into the cause of the fire is currently underway.
key_points: Five people are missing following the fire in Thusis.
Eight people sustained injuries and were taken to various hospitals.
Fourteen people successfully escaped the burning building.
Nearly 100 firefighters responded to the incident after being called just after midnight.
Police and the public prosecutor's office are investigating the cause of the fire.

title: US aircraft carrier arrives in Middle East to relieve troubled USS Lincoln
author: Anna Betts
content:
The USS George Washington aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East, where it is expected to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln from its record deployment amid concerns about poor living conditions and morale.
US Central Command announced on Thursday that the Washington arrived in the area on Wednesday, and posted an image of sailors working on the flight deck as the ship transited the Arabian Sea. No date has yet been announced for the Lincoln to return to the US.
In an interview this week, the wife of a sailor onboard the USS Abraham Lincoln told the Guardian that she has been getting brief glimpses over the past few months of what life is like on the aircraft carrier, mostly through text messages. And that as the deployment has stretched on, and on, she has noticed a change in her husband’s messages.
“There’s less hope in the way he talks and less positive things that he has to say,” she said. “You can just tell the little things.
“He’s just exhausted,” she added. “It’s a long, long deployment and it takes a toll.”
The woman, who spoke on the condition of anonymity out of fear of retribution, said that her husband rarely complained. But photographs he sent of what she described as his sometimes sparse meals as supplies ran low have left her worried. One meal she described as just a “couple of pieces of bacon and three or four chicken wings”.
“He’s never complaining. It’s just when I ask him a question, I’m like, OK, wait a minute, that’s not right,” she said. “To put it plainly, I just don’t think they’re getting enough calories.”
Her account comes as recent reports have rung alarm bells about conditions onboard the Lincoln, which has spent more than 250 days at sea supporting US operations against Iran without a significant port visit or date to return home for the 5,000 sailors aboard.
Reports from families of crew members published in the Navy Times and Stars and Stripes military newspapers described food and water shortages, disrupted mail services, plumbing problems, low morale and worsening mental health, prompting Democratic lawmakers to demand answers from the Pentagon.
“I just don’t really think they’re treating them like people. I think they’re treating them like a uniform, like a pawn on a chessboard,” the wife said in a telephone interview.
Over the weekend, Adm Brad Cooper of US Central Command visited the ship, and released a statement saying the Lincoln “currently has among the lowest number of cases related to mental health” of the navy’s 11 active aircraft carriers, but acknowledged “that doesn’t mean all is perfect”, describing long deployments at sea as “uniquely challenging and tough”.
A navy official, in a statement last week, also recognized that the war had disrupted traditional supply hubs, but said that “current reports from the ship confirm continuous access to clean water, functional [air conditioning] and healthy meal options”.
But the wife of the sailor still worries for her husband and his shipmates.
“He has not point-blank said anything, but I feel like I can tell through text it’s getting hard … being deployed without having any stops, and just kind of doing the same thing over and over again for months is exhausting,” she said, adding: “especially when you’re dealing with high stress” in a war zone.
The couple are in their early 20s and he works on the planes on the flight deck. She said her husband told her that morale among some sailors was low, and that they had been unable to receive packages from home for some time, but she believes the sailors are reluctant to speak out because they fear the consequences for their careers.
“It’s not the sailors that are complaining. It’s their family members who are saying: ‘Whoa, whoa, whoa.’ They are the ones putting their foot down,” she said.
Carl Otis Schuster, a retired US navy captain, said he thought more attention should be paid to the “human element” of these deployments, adding that “until we do that, you’re going to have repeats” of the kinds of problems that have emerged.
“Unfortunately, we’ve made a habit of placing the sacrifices on the crewmen,” Schuster said. “Every generation says that this generation is soft, but I would argue the guys serving on the Abraham Lincoln have undergone stresses and strains that my generation rarely faced, and certainly I never faced.” Schuster served for 26 years on various US and allied warships.
The Lincoln’s crew, he said, had “shown really strong resilience”. During his own service, he said, he never spent more than 90 days at sea, and warned: “All of us have a breaking point.”
He said that typically about 70% of the crew on a ship like the Lincoln are age 26 or younger, living and working together in a confined space.
“We have one carrier fulfilling the mission that would normally be done by two, so there’s nowhere to rotate them out, and so the tension and stress on the crew grows,” he said.
Asked about Donald Trump’s comments last Friday that the Lincoln’s deployment was “not nearly long enough”, Schuster said that the US president may be correct strategically that the US needs a carrier in the region for longer, but that the statement “ignores the human element”, which he said was “everything”.
Lory Manning, who served more than 25 years in the navy, said that sailors typically leave for deployments with a sense of when they will be returning and that “every time that is changed, it’s demoralizing”.
Aircraft carriers, she said, were noisy, crowded and constantly operating. Sailors often work long hours, some in warm areas of the ship such as the engine room, where “you might not get much daylight”, and shortages of basic supplies can make prolonged deployments even harder.
“There’s no privacy,” she said. “In a sense, [it can ultimately feel like] you’re in a jail because you’re on this ship and you can’t get off.”
Yet Manning, who after retiring from the navy got involved with work centered on female veterans and women in the military, said that sailors continued to do their jobs despite the strains.
“The work is getting done, the people are doing what they’re supposed to do,” she said.
Still, she wonders what the long-term consequences may be.
“How many of them will re-enlist someday?” she said.
summary: The USS George Washington aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln from its record deployment. The Lincoln has spent over 250 days at sea supporting operations without a significant port visit, sparking concerns from families and lawmakers regarding low morale, mental health strains, and shortages of food and water. While the Navy maintains that the ship has continuous access to clean water and healthy meals, families and retired military officials emphasize the severe human toll of these prolonged, high-stress deployments.
key_points: The USS George Washington arrived in the Middle East on Wednesday to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln.
The USS Abraham Lincoln has spent over 250 days at sea on a record deployment without a significant port visit.
Family members of crew members and military newspapers have reported issues including food and water shortages, plumbing problems, and declining mental health among the 5,000 sailors aboard.

US Central Command and Navy officials acknowledged the challenging nature of long deployments but defended the ship's conditions, stating mental health cases are low and basic necessities remain accessible.

title: Ukraine war briefing: Kyiv protest organiser disowns Mykhailo Fedorov’s call for elections
author: Warren Murray
content:
- 
  The leader of weeks of protests against Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s sacking of Mykhailo Fedorov as defence minister appeared to call them off after Fedorov demanded elections. The pro-Fedorov movement’s chief organiser, veteran combat medic Dmytro Koziatynskyi, said he “cannot imagine” how to hold polls with troops at the front and the protests had been about seeking dialogue with the government. Elections are considered impossible and illegal under Ukrainian law because of the war.
- 
  “I’m also deeply concerned about the societal divisions during the election process and how that could affect the course of the war,” Koziatynskyi said. “In any case, street protests are definitely not the place for electoral discourse.” The Reuters news agency said that on Wednesday only a few dozen people remained in a central Kyiv square where thousands once protested. “When we came out to protest, we did not come with the idea that elections should be held,” said 22-year-old Iryna Vasyliaka. “That is not what we were here for.”
- 
  Fedorov’s call for elections appeared to be a clumsy misstep, one opposition lawmaker told Reuters. “This demonstrates that [Fedorov] doesn’t have a presidential-level feel for the country.” Olena Prokopenko from the German Marshall Fund said Fedorov’s move was a “false start” that could burn his political capital before elections would realistically be held. “With this statement, he pretty much played on Ukrainians’ most sensitive pain points.” Ukraine’s parliament this week strongly endorsed Zelenskyy’s new defence minister and Fedorov’s successor, Yevhenii Khmara; but the protests did force Ukraine’s president to replace Oleksandr Syrskyi, the disliked “Soviet-style” head of Ukraine’s military, with a younger military reformer, Mykhailo Drapatyi.
- 
  Ukraine reeled on Thursday from a heavy Russian missile and drone bombardment that killed at least 16 people in and around Kyiv in one of the most intense aerial attacks on Ukraine’s capital since the start of the war. Vitali Klitschko, the city’s mayor, said homes, a school and a children’s medical centre were among the buildings damaged in an attack that began at about midnight and continued throughout the day. Volodymr Zelenskyy urged a global response to the attacks. “While Moscow is investing in ballistic missiles and escalation, such strikes do not always receive the response they should. And as long as Ukraine does not have enough anti-ballistic defence, Russia will not consider peace seriously.”
- 
  A Romanian F-16 fighter jet on Thursday destroyed an explosives-laden Russian marine drone near an offshore gas project. “I strongly condemn the escalation of such irresponsible incidents on the part of the Russian Federation,” said the Romanian president, Nicușor Dan. The drone had been “loaded with explosives” and did not originate from Ukraine, said Romania’s defence minister, Radu Miruță. Hundreds of people are working at the gas project, Neptun Deep, according to Romania’s government. Neptun Deep is due to start production in 2027. Nato has shot down four aerial drones in Romania recently.
- 
  Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission chief, slammed the “hybrid warfare” campaign by Russia against the EU after the marine drone incident. “An escalating campaign of threats is under way, unsettling our citizens and seeking to divide our union,” von der Leyen said, warning the EU must step up its defence push to be able to “deter provocation and aggression”.
- 
  Poland on Thursday announced the arrest of a Ukrainian man suspected of an attempt in Kyiv to assassinate a representative of Ukraine’s arms industry on behalf of Russian intelligence services. “The investigation revealed that Serhii P planted an improvised explosive device under a car used by a potential victim,” said Poland’s internal security agency, the ABW. “The device was intended to be detonated remotely using a cellphone. The mechanism did not detonate due to a malfunction.” The suspect fled to Poland where he was arrested in Warsaw. He was charged with attempted murder using explosives and illegal possession of explosives.
- 
  Ukraine’s military hit Russia’s Taneco oil refinery in the Tatarstan region, as well as the Tamanneftegaz oil terminal in the Krasnodar region, the Ukrainian General Staff said on Thursday. The strikes caused fires at both sites. Disgruntled motorists in Moscow are sitting for hours in gasoline station queues of up to a kilometres to fill their cars with rationed amounts of fuel, Reuters reported. Videos showed fistfights erupting at the pumps, as Vladimir Putin’s regime reportedly ordered that people who complain about the shortages face fines and arrest. “We have been to five petrol stations already and there was no fuel. Last week, fuel was available. And now, there is no fuel again,” one Moscow resident told Reuters.
- 
  Russia attacked gas infrastructure in Ukraine’s northern Chernihiv region as well as a border crossing with Moldova in the southern Odesa region,  Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.
summary: Protests in Kyiv against the dismissal of defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov ended after Fedorov called for elections, which organizers rejected as illegal and dangerous during wartime. Meanwhile, Ukraine suffered a heavy Russian missile and drone bombardment resulting in multiple deaths, and Ukrainian forces targeted Russian energy infrastructure, including an oil refinery and terminal. Additionally, a Romanian F-16 destroyed an explosive Russian marine drone near a gas project, and Polish authorities arrested a Ukrainian man suspected of plotting an assassination on behalf of Russian intelligence.
key_points: Protest organizers in Kyiv distanced themselves from Mykhailo Fedorov's call for elections, stating that polls are currently impossible and street protests are not for electoral discourse.
A massive Russian missile and drone attack killed at least 16 people in and around Kyiv and damaged homes, a school, and a children's medical centre.
A Romanian F-16 fighter jet destroyed an explosives-laden Russian marine drone near the Neptun Deep offshore gas project in Romania.
Poland arrested a Ukrainian man in Warsaw suspected of attempting to assassinate a Ukrainian arms industry representative on behalf of Russian intelligence.
Ukrainian military strikes caused fires at Russia's Taneco oil refinery and Tamanneftegaz oil terminal, leading to fuel shortages and queues in Moscow.

title: US Treasury secretary says new economic measures will ‘collapse’ Iran
author: Al Jazeera Staff
content:
![US Secretary of Treasury Scott Bessent speaks to the press outside the West Wing of the White House in Washington, DC, on August 20, 2026.](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/afp_6a872dad556d-1787243949.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has said that a new series of economic measures will “collapse” the Iranian government, calling on countries to join the effort.
Bessent told the news service CNBC on Thursday that the US would apply the “toughest sanctions in history” on Iran, its adversary in a nearly six-month-long war.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3How China and Russia could hobble Trump’s plans to isolate Iran
- list 2 of 3‘Tremendous costs’: Can Trump stop other countries from trading with Iran?
- list 3 of 3Are ships passing Hormuz more willing to defy Iran or US? What data shows
“It is a one-two punch. We have the blockade [on Iran], and we are going to have the toughest sanctions in history,” Bessent said. “It is going to work in Iran, and we are going to collapse this regime.”
He then offered a warning to the members of the international community that they too could face economic penalties if they continue to trade with Iran.
“We’re going to them and saying: You’re either with us or against us,” Bessent said. “If you insist on doing business with them — either transferring money, buying oil, doing seaborne ship transport — then the US Treasury and the US government, they will put its full might and force towards enforcing against you.”
He billed the US’s strategy as the “greatest coordinated economic isolation in the history of the world”.
“It is time for our allies and the rest of the world to make a decision,” Bessent added.
The secretary’s comments follow an announcement from US President Donald Trump a day earlier, promising “the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country” would be unleashed on Iran.
He also threatened “tremendous consequences” for any country that continues to engage economically with Iran.
But what form such penalties could take – and whether they would be applied to powerful countries like China – remains to be seen.
Asked whether China would be targeted, Bessent declined to give a direct answer on Thursday, saying instead that some conversations are best conducted “in private”.
He suggested that all countries should share an interest in isolating Iran, citing the economic impact of Iran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial route for the export of Middle Eastern oil.
Iranian forces have restricted passage since the war began on February 28, when the US and Israel launched an initial volley of attacks.
Prior to the war, traffic flowed freely through the waterway. Reopening the strait has since become a key US aim in ceasefire negotiations, with global oil prices rising since the start of the war.
The conflict has also spurred tensions between the US and its allies, many of whom declined to participate directly in the war effort. Trump has repeatedly lashed out at those countries for not doing enough to help.
Bessent on Thursday reiterated the Trump administration’s position that defeating Iran would have benefits for countries the world over.
“We are confident that everyone wants the strait reopened, and for energy prices to come back down,” Bessent said. “Keep in mind that the Chinese get 50 percent … of their energy from inside the Gulf. So it would do them a big service to get with the programme.”
The US has long sought to isolate and weaken Iran, even before the start of the current war.
On Thursday, for instance, the Trump administration expanded the sanctions against Iran and its allies by designating 10 people associated with Hezbollah, the Iran-backed Lebanese group.
Among the 10 targeted for sanctions was a Turkish businessman, accused of helping to funnel funds to Hezbollah’s base.
But while decades of sanctions have weakened Iran and its allies, critics have been sceptical of their effectiveness in achieving US priorities in Iran, like regime change.
summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that the United States will implement a blockade and the toughest sanctions in history to collapse the Iranian government. He warned that international countries continuing to trade, transfer money, or buy oil from Iran will face economic penalties. The strategy aims to economically isolate Iran and pressure nations to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which has been restricted by Iranian forces since the war began.
key_points: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that new economic measures and a blockade will collapse the Iranian regime.
The US plans to enforce the toughest sanctions in history and warned international countries against trading with Iran.
President Donald Trump's administration aims to achieve the greatest coordinated economic isolation in the world.
Reopening the Strait of Hormuz to lower global oil prices is a key US objective in the strategy.
The Trump administration recently expanded sanctions by targeting 10 individuals, including a Turkish businessman associated with Hezbollah.

title: Woman, 38, posed as 12-year-old using teddy and high child's voice
author: Barney Davis
content:
![Amanda Maria Souza de Oliveira posing as a 12-year-old teenager, undated. She was arrested. (Newsflash/NX)](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308893462-f333.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
A woman has been arrested for posing as a child and tricking a couple into looking after her for more than a year.
Amanda Maria Souza de Oliveira allegedly scammed the couple to get her own bedroom filled with toys and even throw a ’12th birthday party’ for her despite being 38.
She was charged with fraud and false identity for allegedly moving in to to the family’s home for 14 months disguising herself as a vulnerable girl 26 year’s younger.
A hearing at Joinville, in northern Santa Catarina, Brazil heard from the couple who had taken Amanda in, their son, a police officer, experts and two professionals presented by the defence.
Prosecutors accused Amanda of creating the identity of Gabriele Ferreira dos Santos and initially presenting herself as 11 before claiming she was 12.
She had allegedly approached a religious community after claiming she had fled home after being mistreated and had no ID on her.
Sign up for all of the latest stories
![Picture shows the 37-year-old woman suspected of posing as a 12-year-old teenager in Joinville in the North of Santa Catarina, Brazil. (Newsflash/NX)](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308893356-8c2e.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
(Picture: Newsflash/NX)
The family believed they were helping a traumatised child and eventually treated her as a daughter, preparing a bedroom decorated with children’s paintings and paying for her to live.
They even organised a party to celebrate what they believed was her 12th birthday.
According to investigators, Amanda used an infantilised voice, children’s toys, pacifiers and baby bottles to maintain the alleged deception.
She also claimed to have autism and said her adult appearance was the result of being forcibly given hormones during childhood.
Amanda admitted lying about who she was but denied that she had intended to defraud anyone.
According to police, she said: ‘It is clear that I deceived people, I lied. But I did not intend to scam anyone.’
![Picture shows the 37-year-old woman suspected of posing as a 12-year-old teenager in Joinville in the North of Santa Catarina, Brazil. (Newsflash/NX)](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308893359-7ff8.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
(Picture: Newsflash/NX)
Her defence lawyer Lucio Sousa argued during the opening of the trial that Amanda had not caused financial losses and said the identity was instead a survival strategy.
Sousa said: ‘It was the way she found to survive. But she has been a vulnerable person for more than 20 years.’
He added that there had been no allegation that Amanda had obtained financial advantage through robbery or theft, arguing that the elements of fraud had not been established.
Amanda’s lawyer Sarita de Paiva told reporters she had told investigators that she was seeking the attention, affection and protection missing from her childhood.
De Paiva also said that Amanda believed revealing she was an adult would mean she would no longer receive the same care.
But police said the Joinville case was only the latest in a pattern dating back more than a decade.
Social worker Delma Soares said Amanda had stayed with her in Belo Horizonte in 2017 while using the name Karolina and presenting herself as a vulnerable teenager.
Delma said Amanda contacted her after a presentation and asked whether she helped people affected by prostitution and child abuse.
Delma said: ‘She had the posture and behaviour of a teenager.
‘She liked to wear children’s clothes with childish designs.’
The social worker later became suspicious, saying Amanda’s physical strength and sudden changes in behaviour did not fit the age she claimed.
Delma said: ‘When I said she was an adult, people thought I was mistaken.
‘I had no proof, only the conviction I had built through living with her.’
Amanda had reportedly arrived at the project with injuries caused by needles and pieces of wire and was taken to hospital, where examinations found objects in her body.
Another alleged victim, nutritionist Renata Magalhaes, said Amanda used the name Duda when they met in Rio de Janeiro in 2023 and claimed to be an autistic teenager who had suffered abuse.
Renata said the alleged deception was carefully constructed using childish behaviour, drawings and emotional episodes.
Renata said: ‘Her phone was full of searches. She researched how an autistic person behaves and how to make drawings to move evangelical people.’
Renata also alleged that Amanda had inserted needles into herself and later vomited them in front of her.
Renata said: ‘She vomited the needle. She vomited, she did it in front of me. It is bizarre.’
She added: ‘I have seen many people laughing and making jokes on the internet, but she is a fraudster, a narcissist, a dangerous woman. She is a person who puts on a character like a coat and creates a totally fake narrative.’
A psychologist who encountered Amanda in Recife in 2023 said she also carried a teddy bear, spoke in a childlike voice and claimed to have suffered sexual abuse.
The psychologist said: ‘She demonstrated childish behaviour in her body language and an infantilised voice, but we could see the traits of an adult woman.
‘We could see there was a performance there; it was not something genuine or natural.’
Amanda also allegedly used another identity, Emily, in Parana during the Covid-19 pandemic, claiming to be a 13-year-old girl suffering from terminal leukaemia.
- 
	![A screen grab of the Royal Shalimar on Highgate Road, Birmingham showing a car on fire.](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/110746993-0-image-m-38_1787216239268.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=636&h=358&crop=1)
- Teens killed in wrong-way crash 'had been terrorising communities for weeks'
- CEO who fired 900 employees on Zoom before Christmas now upset he’s been fired
- Soap opera spoilers: Harry and Meghan in shock return
One woman who became emotionally attached to the supposed child reportedly even had the name Emily tattooed on her wrist.
In another case in Jundiai, Sao Paulo, in 2022, Amanda allegedly identified herself as Ana Clara dos Santos Oliveira, claimed to have been born in 2009 and told authorities she had escaped a house of prostitution where she had allegedly been sexually exploited since childhood.
Amanda was arrested at the Joinville family’s home on June 2 and has remained in custody since then.
The judge said the request for Amanda’s release would be considered alongside the verdict, which is expected within five days.
summary: A 38-year-old woman named Amanda Maria Souza de Oliveira was arrested in Joinville, Brazil, after spending 14 months posing as a vulnerable 12-year-old girl and tricking a family into taking her in. Investigators and witnesses revealed a pattern spanning over a decade where she used false identities, a childlike voice, toys, and fabricated stories of abuse to manipulate people into caring for her. While Amanda admitted to lying, her defense argued she did not intend to commit fraud and used the persona as a survival strategy, whereas police and other victims described her as a dangerous fraudster.
key_points: Amanda Maria Souza de Oliveira, 38, was arrested and charged with fraud and false identity for posing as a 12-year-old child.
She lived with a family in Joinville for 14 months, who treated her like a daughter, decorated a bedroom for her, and threw her a birthday party.
Investigators stated she used an infantilized voice, children's toys, pacifiers, and false claims of autism and abuse to maintain the deception.
Witnesses and social workers reported similar past incidents dating back over a decade where she used different fake identities and child personas across multiple locations in Brazil.

title: Missing teenager found dead after police said she was alive
author: Milo Pope
content:
A missing teenager has been found dead after officials mistakenly announced that she had been rescued following an eight-day search in the Australian bushland.
Lily Hooper, 18, disappeared after setting off for a hike in Nattai National Park, around 90 miles south-west of Sydney, last Wednesday.
Her family raised the alarm after she failed to return home, despite her being in contact with them throughout the day.
A major search operation was then launched in the national park, with police, volunteers and around 100 soldiers.
On Thursday, New South Wales premier Chris Minns was attending a parliamentary hearing when he was handed a note telling him the teenager had been found.
![Lily Hooper Search](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308700111-3961-e1787227074452.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
Sign up for all of the latest stories
He then announced the news to the room, saying: ‘We’ve got some fantastic news, Mr Chair – Lily Hooper has been found alive.’
After claiming that she had been found in the bush with half a bottle of water, the apparent rescue was quickly reported by media outlets in Australia.
However, shortly afterwards, Minns confirmed that his announcement was incorrect, as he said: ‘I’ve got some terrible news. It seems as if the earlier advice was wrong.
‘Lily’s body has been found. This is obviously devastating and I’m just profoundly sad for her family and all those concerned.’
![Lily Hooper Search](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308700106-736a-e1787227170886.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
Lily had originally left her home in Oakdale, near Sydney, at 8am on August 12.
Her car was found at 11pm the same day in a picnic ground at the base of Bonnum Pic, which is a walking trail for experienced hikers.
![16051471 Urgent search for missing Aussie](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308240252-a907.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
The area is covered by dense eucalyptus forest, sandstone cliffs and deep ravines, with rescuers describing the terrain as ‘incredibly rough’.
Lily’s family had also joined the search as rescuers remained hopeful that her experience in the bush would help her survive.
![Lily Hooper Search](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308700117-b509.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
On Thursday, ambulances were then sent to the bushland after rescuers reported finding a person in the bushland.
New South Wales Police assistant commissioner Joseph Cassar said Lily’s parents had initially been told rescuers believed their daughter had been found alive.
Cassar said volunteers searching through the thick terrain were dealing with communication difficulties and had contacted the command post after locating her.
However, an updated report was sent around eight to 10 minutes later, confirming that she had died, with Lily’s parents then being informed.
- 
	![16060309 Alex McCarthy died in the collision in Co Kildare in the early hours of Sunday morningAlex McCarthyFor Dan Sanderson](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308733309-7680.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646&h=363&crop=1)
- Row of supercars petrol bombed during wedding in Birmingham
- CEO who fired 900 employees on Zoom before Christmas now upset he’s been fired
- Soap opera spoilers: Harry and Meghan in shock return
‘If we were able to provide them more detailed information on that first report, I can tell you that would have been the case,’ Cassar said.
‘If I could turn the clock back, I would certainly.’
Police and government officials are now investigating how the incorrect information was passed on.
New South Wales Police said the woman’s body found in the search area had yet to be formally identified, but it is believed to be that of Lily’s. Police will now also prepare a report for the coroner.
summary: An 18-year-old missing teenager named Lily Hooper was found dead in the Australian bushland following an eight-day search. The New South Wales premier initially announced she had been rescued alive after receiving incorrect information, but quickly retracted the statement. Police and government officials are currently investigating how the false report was initially passed on to authorities.
key_points: Lily Hooper disappeared after going for a hike in Nattai National Park in Australia.
A major search operation involving police, volunteers, and soldiers was launched after she failed to return home.
NSW Premier Chris Minns mistakenly announced she was found alive before correcting the statement to confirm her body was found.
Communication difficulties in the rough terrain contributed to the initial false report given to authorities and her parents.
Police are preparing a report for the coroner regarding the death.

title: UK, France, Germany, Italy and Canada condemn Israel's West Bank settlement project
author: Ruth Comerford; Tom McArthur
content:
![Wide view of a highway near the Israeli settlement of Maale Adumim in the area of the so-called E1 project in Jerusalem, in the occupied West Bank, taken in February 2026.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/980/cpsprodpb/e405/live/b1ef1300-9be4-11f1-ba30-ddd78081057f.jpg)
File photo of the Israeli settlement of Maale Adumim in the occupied West Bank next to the so-called E1 project in East Jerusalem, taken in February 2026
- Published
Israel's plans to open up tenders for the construction of some 1,200 settlement homes in a strategically important part of the occupied West Bank have sparked fresh condemnation by major Western powers.
In a joint statement, the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Canada called the decision "unacceptable", external and urged Israel to "retract the plans immediately".
All settlements are illegal under international law and, under international pressure, Israel held off for decades on plans to build in E1 to the east of Jerusalem.
Many of its allies and Palestinians argued this development would deal a major blow to hopes of a two-state solution, effectively cutting the West Bank in two and isolating east Jerusalem.
"At a time of grave instability in the West Bank with unprecedented levels of violence by settlers against civilians, and serious restrictions on the Palestinian economy, this decision is even more concerning", the statement from the European allies and Canada published on Thursday said.
"Not only will they [the plans] take us further from peace, but they further undermine Israel's international standing," the statement added.
In a separate statement, the UN secretary general also said the E1 plan posed an "existential threat" to a contiguous Palestinian state - and so did Belgium's foreign minister.
UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband's condemnation earlier on Thursday had drawn "ouright" rejection by the Israeli foreign minister.
![Map showing Israeli settlements and built-up Palestinian areas in the West Bank around Jerusalem â highlighting the E1 settlement in red. Other Israeli settlements are marked in blue and Palestinian areas in light purple. The municipal boundary of Jerusalem is outlined in red. An inset map shows the regionâs location within Israel and Jordan.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1280/cpsprodpb/48fd/live/00ce0160-790a-11f0-a20f-3b86f375586a.png)
Despite an Israeli court challenge to the plans by Bedouin Palestinians living in the area and Israeli peace groups, on Wednesday the Israeli housing ministry issued a tender for 1,234 of the 3,401 housing units approved by the Israeli government last August.
It covers about 12 sq km (4.6 sq miles) between East Jerusalem and the settlement of Maale Adumim.
At the time of their unveiling, Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich - an ultranationalist and settler - said the idea of a Palestinian state was "being erased".
The deadline for bids is 19 October, just days before Israel's general election on 27 October, making it much harder for any future government to overturn any tenders issued.
Israel has built about 160 settlements housing 700,000 Jews since it occupied the West Bank and East Jerusalem - land Palestinians want, along with Gaza, for a hoped-for future state - during the 1967 Middle East war. An estimated 3.3 million Palestinians live alongside them.
Despite the fierce international opposition, successive Israeli governments have allowed settlements to grow.
However, expansion has risen sharply since Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu returned to power in late 2022 at the head of a right-wing, pro-settler coalition, as well as the start of the Gaza war, triggered by Hamas's 7 October 2023 attack on Israel.
Opponents of the E1 project have warned that it would effectively block the establishment of a Palestinian state because it would cut off the north of the West Bank from the south, and prevent the development in the centre of a contiguous Palestinian urban area connecting Ramallah, East Jerusalem and Bethlehem.
- ![Wide view of a highway near the Israeli settlement of Maale Adumim in the area of the so-called E1 project in Jerusalem, in the occupied West Bank, taken in February 2026.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/980/cpsprodpb/e405/live/b1ef1300-9be4-11f1-ba30-ddd78081057f.jpg)
  - Published1 August
 ![Yehuda Shimon, a large, bearded man wearing glasses, gestures with his hand](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1280/cpsprodpb/678b/live/ea29f390-8c56-11f1-b8ee-9b3c26ad07bb.jpg)
summary: Major Western powers, including the UK, France, Germany, Italy, and Canada, have strongly condemned Israel's plans to open tenders for building settlement homes in the E1 area of the occupied West Bank. Critics warn that the project would cut the West Bank in two, isolate East Jerusalem, and severely damage the prospects of a two-state solution. Despite international opposition and legal challenges, the Israeli housing ministry issued a tender for over 1,200 housing units.
key_points: The UK, France, Germany, Italy, and Canada issued a joint statement calling Israel's E1 settlement plans unacceptable and urging an immediate retraction.
The Israeli housing ministry issued tenders for 1,234 housing units between East Jerusalem and the Maale Adumim settlement.
Opponents and international allies warn the E1 project threatens a contiguous Palestinian state by cutting the West Bank in half.
All settlements are considered illegal under international law, though Israel disputes this.

title: Melania Trump kicks off public appearance in a month with tongue-in-cheek joke
author: Alex Woodward
content:
First Lady Melania Trump made her first public appearance in more than a month as she delivered remarks from the White House to tout her foster care initiative.
“Good afternoon. I heard you missed me,” she said as she addressed a crowd at the Rose Garden on Thursday. “Here I am.”
President Donald Trump held her hand as she walked her towards a lectern to deliver her remarks and then patted her on the back.
The first lady has remained largely out of the spotlight with her husband’s return to the White House. She has made even fewer public appearances in the president’s second term than his first; her last public appearance was at the 2026 World Cup final on July 19.
Melania Trump did not join the president to attend the dignified transfer of the remains of four dead U.S. service members, nor did she sit beside the president at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner two days later on July 24. She also did not attend Senator Lindsey Graham’s funeral on July 28.
An analysis from The Daily Beast determined Melania Trump, until her appearance at the White House on Thursday, had appeared in public only 38 days this year.
Trump aide Natalie Harp, meanwhile, has seldom strayed far from the president’s side.
The ubiquitous presence of the 35-year-old executive assistant within the president’s inner circle has come under intense scrutiny following reports that she was among a small group of top aides who secretly joined Trump aboard a military aircraft departing a NATO summit in Turkey this summer.
The former One America News Network personality reportedly declined to obtain security clearance for more than a year after she started working at the White House and repeatedly received extensions to complete the paperwork that would require her to disclose her financial history, prior residences and foreign contacts.
Recent remarks from Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff — who said Trump “doesn’t want to do the job” of president but would rather build a highly contentious White House ballroom and “travel with Natalie” — sparked a fierce defense of Harp’s presence from the president’s allies while amplifying questions about her role at the White House.
Harp, who earned her “printer” nickname after routinely handing Trump large-format printouts of news articles and social media posts, has has also reportedly provided the president with deeply personal “devotional letters.”
The first lady — in partnership with IndyCar and the Fox Corporation as the president launches a Grand Prix race in Washington, D.C. — announced the launch of a new scholarship program for young adults transitioning out of foster care.
Her “Fostering the Future” initiative is being supported by a $2 million donation from the companies to fund scholarships at Indiana University and Purdue University, according to the White House. The partnership expands the program’s network to 26 academic institutions.
“America's greatest competitive advantage remains in its own people,” she said in prepared remarks. “Tomorrow’s leaders are sitting in classrooms today, including those growing up in foster care. Their capability is no less remarkable.”
Though she only made two public appearances in July, the first lady’s office announced on July 30 that she helped reunite five Ukrainian and Russian children with their families who were displaced during the ongoing war.
"While diplomacy and peacebuilding are important to this effort, they are surpassed by our collective ability to place children above international disputes," she said in a statement at the time. “Every reunion is a reminder that compassion, dignity, and family can transcend even the darkest of times: war."
Though she made several other appearances in Washington, D.C., this year, including congressional hearings on foster care and at a White House event for students who participated in an artificial intelligence challenge, one of her most high-profile addresses was also something of a surprise.
In April, she delivered a remarkable five-minute address from the White House to deny any connection to Jeffrey Epstein while condemning what she called “unfounded and baseless lies” and “false smears” against her from “politically motivated individuals and entities” who have sought to “gain financially and climb politically.”
Such statements, she pleaded, “must stop.”
summary: First Lady Melania Trump made her first public appearance in over a month during a White House Rose Garden event to promote her foster care initiative. Opening with a tongue-in-cheek joke, she announced a $2 million partnership providing scholarships for young adults transitioning out of foster care. Her rare public appearances this year have contrasted with intense scrutiny surrounding presidential aide Natalie Harp.
key_points: Melania Trump made her first public appearance in over a month to announce an expansion of her foster care initiative.
The 'Fostering the Future' initiative received a $2 million donation to fund scholarships at Indiana University and Purdue University.
Presidential aide Natalie Harp has faced scrutiny regarding her White House role and security clearance extensions.
Melania Trump previously delivered an April address denying connections to Jeffrey Epstein and helped reunite displaced Ukrainian and Russian children in July.

title: Trump administration faces questions over top aide Natalie Harp’s security clearance
author: Joseph Gedeon; David Smith
content:
The White House faced fresh questions on Thursday over whether Donald Trump’s closest aide, Natalie Harp, had access to US government secrets without security clearance.
Harp, who is executive assistant to the US president, worked at the White House for a year without the routine clearance, the MS Now network reported on Thursday. She refused to file the relevant forms for unknown reasons, according to two unnamed sources cited by MS Now.
It was only when the White House counsel’s office raised the issue, and when Trump himself became involved, that Harp filled out the paperwork for a federal background investigation and was belatedly granted clearance, according to the report.
Norm Eisen, a former White House ethics tsar, said: “It is shocking that an aide who has potential exposure to the nation’s most sensitive secrets reportedly went without a security clearance for so long. Treating access to confidences as a casual job perk is an outrageous way to handle our national security.”
Eisen, co-founder of Democracy Defenders Action, a non-partisan group dedicated to free and fair elections, added: “This is the continued incompetence of an administration willing to set aside our country’s interests, ignore established protocol, and make the White House vulnerable to intelligence risks in order to appease Trump. The American people deserve answers.”
Harp’s influence has come under close scrutiny this week after her name was invoked by Jon Ossoff, a Democratic US senator for Georgia.
Harp has reportedly sent the US president adoring letters, helps him write social media posts, and has been dubbed “the human printer” because she supplies him with printouts of favourable coverage.
The MS Now report about her prolonged lack of security clearance drew criticism of the arrangement among former White House officials across the political spectrum.
In response, the White House press secretary, Karoline Leavitt, said in a statement: “Natalie Harp has a security clearance like everyone else, and she is a loyal and hardworking member of President Trump’s team.”
David Axelrod, who was chief strategist and senior adviser to Barack Obama, posted on X: “If this story is true, and the person closest to the @POTUS and his thinking on a daily basis has no security clearance and refuses to submit to the process of getting it, it’s a deadly serious issue.”
Richard Painter, a former chief ethics lawyer for George W Bush, noted that all White House staff usually undergo a background investigation, but only some require additional security clearance, depending on their access to classified information. “I’m not entirely clear what has been going on here with Natalie Harp,” he said. “My sense of most of what she’s doing has nothing to do with classified information.”
But Painter added: “If she is accompanying the president on his trips in Air Force One, in a proximity where she can overhear conversations that could include classified information, she needs to have the security clearance.
“You could be in a situation where, if the president wants her on his trips, and he’s in Air Force One, and he is on the phone, and she’s sitting in the cabin there because she’s doing something else, even if she doesn’t give advice on how to handle Iran and he’s on the phone talking about the next strike on Iran, right then and there she needs a security clearance.”
‘A disturbing trend’
The prospect of a potential security vetting lapse involving those closest to Trump carries echoes of Trump’s first term, Donald K Sherman, the president of the legal advocacy group Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, said.
“In his first administration, Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner was only granted a clearance after Trump ordered it, overruling concerns raised by intelligence officials,” Sherman said. “Too often, the president has given more flexibility with security clearances to those closest to him, which is a disturbing trend given the kind of sensitive information they may have access to, like national security information, contacts with world leaders, and other highly confidential information.”
Rick Wilson, a co-founder of the Lincoln Project, an anti-Trump group, said: “It’s unsurprising that Donald Trump, who couldn’t pass a credit check, never mind a security check, would have no problem letting someone without clearance be in such a sensitive position for a year.
“This is after all, a guy who meets with Putin without any aides and praises Kim Jong-un. Natalie’s all-consuming fanatical devotion and willingness to be at Trump’s side whenever he needs plays into his pathological need for attention.”
Harp, 35, first came to national attention as a cancer survivor and enthusiastic Trump supporter who spoke at the 2020 Republican national convention in Washington. She joined the far-right One America News Network in 2020 and went to work for Trump two years later as he plotted his political resurrection.
She has frequently been at his side ever since. The CNN network reported that in 2023, when Trump was due to appear in court in New York, Harp discovered there was no seat for her in his motorcade so she jumped into the trunk of an SUV, insisting that he had personally asked her to attend.
And last month, when Trump secretly switched aircraft in Turkey after an alleged Iranian assassination threat, Harp was among a small group who accompanied him on a military aircraft while other officials and journalists remained onboard a decoy Air Force One.
This week Ossoff attacked Trump in a campaign speech, accusing him of being more interested in building his White House ballroom and travelling with “Natalie” than carrying out the duties of president.
The remark prompted an extraordinary backlash from the White House and sent social media into overdrive, with users speculating about the nature of Harp’s relationship with Trump.
Her loyalty to the president has also been documented in the book Regime Change, published this year by the New York Times reporters Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan. They reported that Harp had written Trump intensely admiring letters, including one in which she told him: “You are all that matters to me.”
summary: The White House faced questions after reports emerged that top presidential aide Natalie Harp worked for a year without routine security clearance. According to reports, Harp refused to file background check forms until the White House counsel and Donald Trump intervened. Ethics experts and former officials criticized the situation, citing national security risks, while the White House maintained that Harp has a security clearance like everyone else.
key_points: Natalie Harp reportedly worked as Donald Trump's executive assistant for a year without undergoing routine security clearance background checks.
The White House counsel's office and Trump reportedly had to intervene before Harp finally filled out the necessary paperwork.
Ethics experts and former officials criticized the delay, warning that close proximity to the president on trips like Air Force One poses national security risks.
White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt defended Harp, stating that she has a security clearance and is a hardworking member of the team.
