title: German neo-Nazi suspected of deadly 1970 arson at Jewish retirement home
author: Paul Kirby
content:
![Women mourn the victims in a black and white photo showing coffins](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/8cda/live/49f9c620-9c87-11f1-95d8-5b0dba89a322.jpg)
The arson attack has long been seen as one of the worst attacks targeting Germany's post-war Jewish community
- Published
German investigators believe they have now identified an arsonist who set fire to a Jewish community centre in Munich in 1970, killing seven people.
For decades the man's identity remained a mystery. But Munich prosecutors now believe he was a 25-year-old lone neo-Nazi with known antisemitic opinions.
The seven killed were all Holocaust survivors aged 59 to 71. Another 15 people were injured.
The prosecutors' revelations come too late to secure justice for the victims. The suspect, identified by Der Spiegel magazine as Bernd V, died in 2020.
At about 20:40 on 13 February 1970, prosecutors say the killer poured petrol into the wooden stairwell at a retirement home housed inside the Jewish community building on Reichenbachstrasse, and then set it alight. The fire spread quickly to the top floor of the building.
While many managed to escape to the roof or were rescued by firefighters, four of the victims died in the stairwell and another died after jumping from a window.
Prosecutors now believe they have "compelling grounds pointing to the (deceased) suspect being the perpetrator", based on "credible information" from a woman, who came forward last year after the death of a close relative who had known the man well.
According to prosecutors, the suspected killer was heard to claim within the immediate vicinity of the community building that "the Jews had everything" and he wanted to "set them on fire". Fifteen minutes later, the building was engulfed in flames.
Authorities say those remarks have been corroborated by other members of the witness's family. They say other witnesses described the man as having a "Hitler-fixation" - and how he had listened to records of speeches by the Nazi dictator in his youth.
One head teacher told them the suspect had apparently used a Hitler-youth dagger, given to him by his father, during a confrontation. He was later given a juvenile conviction for blowing up two phone kiosks.
Spiegel reports that the female witness's relative had once been a member of a gang of burglars and that on the night of the arson attack on the retirement home they had taken part in a failed raid on a jewellery store in nearby GÃ¤rtnerplatz.
The relative said the botched burglary had infuriated Bernd V and stirred him into an antisemitic rage.
The investigation into the arson attack was closed in 2017 because of a lack of conclusive evidence, before being re-opened last year.
Prosecutors say the presumption of innocence still applies, even after a suspect's death, and they have also said there is no reliable evidence to suggest anyone else was involved in the attack.
Fifty-six years later, German authorities are now confident they have cracked a notorious antisemitic crime.
However, the case will quite likely be seen as a historic failure by police.
Bernd V's name had been brought to the attention of investigators in the early 1970s, according to Spiegel by a man who shared a prison cell with him. But they had insufficient evidence and dropped the case against him some time afterwards.
summary: German prosecutors believe they have identified a 25-year-old lone neo-Nazi as the perpetrator of the deadly 1970 arson attack on a Munich Jewish community centre and retirement home that killed seven Holocaust survivors. The suspect, identified as Bernd V, died in 2020, meaning the findings come too late to secure legal justice. The breakthrough followed information provided by a witness last year after the death of a close relative who knew the suspect.
key_points: The 1970 arson attack killed seven Holocaust survivors aged 59 to 71 and injured 15 others.
The newly identified suspect, Bernd V, died in 2020 at the age of 75.
Prosecutors state the attack was allegedly triggered by an antisemitic rage following a failed burglary on the night of the fire.
The suspect's name had originally been brought to investigators in the early 1970s by a cellmate, but the case was dropped due to insufficient evidence.
The presumption of innocence still applies to the deceased suspect, and no evidence suggests anyone else was involved.

title: Scott Bessent urges US partners to back plans to 'squash' Iran economy
author: Rorey Bosotti
content:
![US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent addresses members of the media on the lawn outside the White House. He's wearing a light grey suit, white shirt and silver tie](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1200/cpsprodpb/f685/live/690551d0-9cc6-11f1-a5cd-a14170183a2c.png)
Bessent believes international sanctions will 'minimise the need' to return to war with Iran
- Published
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged US allies to support Washington's efforts to "squash" the Iranian economy.
"We are going to collapse this regime. It is time for our allies and the rest of the world to make a decision," Bessent told broadcaster CNBC.
"You are either with us or against us," he said.
Bessent's remarks come after US President Donald Trump said that countries providing "any type of lifeline" to the Islamic Republic's regime will face "tremendous economic consequences".
Bessent did not offer any insight on the measures Trump's team was looking to implement, but said the planned pressure campaign on the Iranian economy would minimise the need of a "large-scale kinetic restart" of the conflict.
The US and Israel started a war with Iran in February, arguing the strikes were to prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons, which Tehran has consistently denied.
Iran, however, responded by attacking Israel, US bases across the Middle East as well as targeting Gulf Arab allies of the US.
Since then, Iran has largely closed the Strait of Hormuz - the waterway through which some 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas used to transit - causing wild fluctuations in prices on world markets.
The US and Iran agreed a ceasefire in April - and then another one in June, both aimed at facilitating negotiations to end the conflict.
However, the truce has been consistenly broken and talks appear to have stalled but, instead of returning to war, Trump is gearing up to unleash the "most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country"..
Bessent said the new economic penalties will be part of "the greatest co-ordinated economic isolation in the history of the world".
"If you insist on doing business with them, either transferring money, buying their oil... then the US Treasury and the US government will put [their] full might and force towards enforcing against you," the treasure secretary said referring to the US's international trading partners.
Bessent confirmed further details about the plan will be made public at a press conference on 24 August.
The Iranian economy has long been struggling under the weight of decades of international sanctions, which left it in tatters.
Earlier this year, Iran experienced weeks of protests due to the spiralling cost of living and inflation â with everyday Iranians blaming the regime for their difficulties.
Official figures show that in the 12 months to February 2026, the price of basic necessities increased by an average 60%, while food prices doubled in the same period.
At the time, Trump told demonstrators "help is on the way" as he urged them to "keep protesting".
The attacks on Iran ensued - and later led to the US to imposed a blockade on Iranian ports, threatening further sanctions.
In April, the US launched a wave of sanctions on foreign banks and firms doing business with Tehran after it became apparent military operations had not led to the overthrow of Iran's regime nor its surrender, as Trump had initially hoped.
Operation Economic Fury, announced by the US Treasury Department and the Pentagon in April, aimed at degrading Tehran's warfighting capability by cutting off its revenue streams, and also included a naval blockade aimed at stopping Iranian exports.
The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed by Iran and the US in June included a clause stating that the US would "terminate all types of sanctions" against Iran in an agreed-upon schedule.
One resident in the central Iranian province of Khuzestan told the BBC the country has a long experience with sanctions, and will be able to overcome the additional economic pressure.
"There may be an impact at first, but that doesn't necessarily mean Iran won't be able to overcome the crisis," he said.
Another resident also doubts fresh penalties will have an impact on the longevity of the regime.
"Not everything changes because of statements made by President Trump," she told Middle East Lifeline.
"Iran has been living under sanctions for years, and people have become accustomed to this situation. I'm sure Iran will find other ways to continue trading."
"Of course, there will be some impact and the economy may weaken, but that doesn't mean it will collapse."
summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has called on international allies to support a renewed economic pressure campaign aimed at collapsing Iran's economy and avoiding a return to military conflict. President Donald Trump has warned that nations providing a lifeline to Iran will face severe economic penalties, with further details expected at an August 24 press conference. The planned measures follow a series of broken ceasefires and ongoing tensions between the US and Iran, which has already faced years of crippling sanctions and soaring inflation.
key_points: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged international partners to back US efforts to squash the Iranian economy.
President Donald Trump threatened tremendous economic consequences for countries providing a lifeline to Iran.
Bessent stated that the economic pressure campaign is intended to minimize the need for a large-scale military restart.
Further details regarding the planned economic penalties will be revealed at a press conference on August 24.

title: Romania destroys explosive drone near major Black Sea gas project
author: Simon Ormiston
content:
A separate drone crashed in eastern Romania as the country and neighbouring Poland stepped up air defences during a major Russian attack on Ukraine.
A Romanian F-16 fighter jet has destroyed an explosive-laden maritime drone close to Europe's largest offshore gas project, hours after another drone entered the NATO member's airspace and crashed near the Ukrainian border.
Romania's President Nicuşor Dan blamed Russia for the latest incident and condemned what he called an escalation of "irresponsible incidents" by Moscow.
The maritime drone was spotted by a commercial vessel at 06:28 local time on Thursday, a few hundred metres from work at the Neptun Deep offshore gas project, around 80 nautical miles east of the Romanian city of Constanța.
Two Romanian F-16 fighter jets were scrambled and one destroyed the drone after authorities decided it posed a potential threat to the hundreds of people working at the site and to critical energy infrastructure.
Defence Minister Radu Miruță said the drone was carrying explosives and that Kyiv had confirmed it was not Ukrainian.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen described the incident as part of "an escalating campaign of threats" against the European Union.
"This is hybrid warfare," she said, accusing those responsible of seeking to unsettle European citizens and divide the bloc.
Neptun Deep is one of the largest energy projects under development in the Black Sea and is expected to begin producing natural gas in 2027.
It comes after Romania scrambled NATO fighter jets after a drone entered its airspace during a major Russian missile and drone attack on neighbouring Ukraine.
Romania's Defence Ministry said military radar detected a group of aerial targets close to the Ukrainian border, north of the eastern county of Tulcea, at 02:23 local time on Thursday.
Two Spanish F-18 fighter jets in Romania as part of NATO's air policing mission were scrambled to monitor the situation, while a Romanian IAR-330 SOCAT military helicopter was sent on a reconnaissance mission.
Authorities also issued an alert to people in the affected area.
The ministry said that at 03:21 a drone crossed into Romanian airspace about 13 kilometres east of Galați, a city close to the borders with Ukraine and Moldova.
Three minutes later, the Romanian helicopter crew reported that the drone had crashed about four kilometres north-east of the village of Grindu in Tulcea County.
The impact sparked a fire, which extinguished itself. No casualties or damage were reported and a military team was sent to secure the crash site.
Romania has not yet identified the origin of the drone.
The incident comes just four days after a Spanish F-18 shot down another drone after it entered Romanian airspace from Moldova.
Romania did not identify that aircraft either, although a NATO spokesperson said it appeared to be Russian. At thte time it was reported that it was the fourth drone shot down over Romania this year, after Romanian F-16s intercepted three Russian drones in July.
Romania, a member of both NATO and the European Union, shares a long border with Ukraine and has repeatedly reported Russian drones entering its airspace or debris falling on its territory since Moscow launched its invasion in 2022.
Poland also mobilised military aircraft and activated air defence systems during Thursday's Russian attacks on Ukraine, particularly in areas close to its border.
summary: A Romanian F-16 fighter jet destroyed an explosive-laden maritime drone near the Neptun Deep offshore gas project in the Black Sea. Separately, another drone entered Romanian airspace and crashed near the Ukrainian border during a major Russian attack on Ukraine. Romanian President Nicuşor Dan blamed Russia for the maritime drone incident, condemning an escalation of irresponsible actions by Moscow.
key_points: A Romanian F-16 fighter jet destroyed an explosive maritime drone near the Neptun Deep gas project.
A separate drone entered Romanian airspace and crashed near the Ukrainian border, causing no casualties or damage.
President Nicuşor Dan blamed Russia for the maritime drone incident and escalation.
Poland and Romania both stepped up air defenses during recent Russian attacks on Ukraine.

title: More than 100 dead after goldmine collapses in Central African Republic
author: Eromo Egbejule
content:
More than 100 people have died after an artisanal goldmine at a small village in western Central African Republic (CAR) caved in due to a landslide, local officials and aid workers said on Wednesday.
The landslide happened on Tuesday afternoon in the village of Zamboye, about 50km (31 miles) from the town of Baboua and close to the border of Cameroon. Footage on social media appeared to show an avalanche of sand descend on a group of people, likely the miners, and cover them.
A statement by a local public prosecutor said many others were trapped under the deluge. It did not mention the number of fatalities. However, Gervais Ganagoroh, a Red Cross volunteer involved in the relief effort, told the Associated Press news agency on Wednesday that more than 100 bodies had been recovered from the collapse and a senior official at a local mining association confirmed that number to Reuters.
Local media in CAR reported that authorities had launched an investigation into the incident. A second prosecutor from Baboua told the press that the incident is believed to have been caused by “the collapse of several underground tunnels in which miners were operating”.
“The ground completely collapsed and buried people,” Cedric Mbango, a miner at the site, told the AFP news agency, describing the incident as “catastrophic”.
Rescuers are racing to retrieve the bodies of victims and find survivors among the miners, believed to be nationals of CAR and Cameroon. Authorities in Cameroon’s Eastern region said at least three of its citizens have been identified as victims in the incident.
Grégoire Mvongo, the region’s governor told state-owned radio on Wednesday that he was “working in close collaboration with our Central African colleagues to deal with the aftermath of this tragedy”.
Bertrand Be Yangué, a member of the Zamboye youth council, said that “finding them alive would be a miracle.” He added: “We are saddened and heartbroken to see young men and women perish after coming to the mines to save their families from despair.”
The toll is expected to rise as the rescue efforts continue, added Yangué.
The Central African news website Corbeau News reported that heavy machinery, including tractors, was being used in the retrieval mission and could jeopardise the rescue of those still alive under the landmass.
The exact number of people who were in the mine at the time of the cave-in remains unknown.
Small scale artisanal mines are common in different parts of Africa, despite regulations criminalising them, as unemployment continues to drive able-bodied men to abandoned or unused mines, to eke a living. The mining sites often operate with weak safety standards leading to repeated incidents: at least 40 people have died in several mining incidents in CAR this year alone.
summary: More than 100 people have died following the collapse of an artisanal goldmine in the village of Zamboye in the western Central African Republic. The disaster, caused by a landslide that caved in several underground tunnels on Tuesday, has left many others trapped or missing. Rescuers and local officials are currently working to recover victims and search for potential survivors, though the death toll is expected to rise.
key_points: Over 100 bodies have been recovered following the goldmine collapse in Zamboye.
The landslide and cave-in occurred on Tuesday afternoon near the Cameroon border.
Authorities believe the disaster was caused by the collapse of several underground mining tunnels.
Rescuers are working at the site, though finding further survivors is considered unlikely.
At least 40 people have died in CAR mining incidents this year alone due to weak safety standards.

title: Trump declares ‘economic D-Day’ against Iran
author: Andrea Hamblin
content:
![Strait of Hormuz](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/en-us/news/2026/08/20/TELEMMGLPICT000498771274_17871935129960_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqRo0U4xU-30oDveS4pXV-Vv4Xpit_DMGvdp2n7FDd82k.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Strait of Hormuz](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/en-us/news/2026/08/20/TELEMMGLPICT000498771274_17871935129960_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqRo0U4xU-30oDveS4pXV-Vv4Xpit_DMGvdp2n7FDd82k.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
Donald Trump announced the “most crushing economic operation ever” against Iran as he pivots to financial warfare to try to force Tehran into accepting his terms of a deal to end the war.
The US president declared “economic D-day” in a social media post on Wednesday evening and warned that countries providing “any kind of lifeline” to Iran would also face “tremendous economic consequences”.
“Oil smuggling, swap lines, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries, front companies – it all needs to stop NOW,” Mr Trump said on his Truth Social account.
“You know who you are,” he wrote, without naming any country. “This will be an ECONOMIC D-DAY, and we need all of our Allies to stand with the United States of America to isolate, and defeat, the Iran threat.”
Mr Trump has searched for new ways to threaten Iran as talks to end the US-Iran war and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz remain stalled.
He is said to be unwilling to return to full-scale war, and lacking the means to do so as American weapons stockpiles dwindle.
The president is also facing growing disquiet over his handling of the war at a time Republicans are trying to gain support before the Midterms. A July poll showed just 28 per cent of Americans approve of his approach to the conflict.
“No one has given the Islamic Republic of Iran a greater opportunity to make a Deal than me,” Mr Trump wrote on Wednesday.
“TRAGICALLY, for them, they have failed to take it. Therefore, today, I am announcing the MOST CRUSHING ECONOMIC OPERATION EVER TAKEN AGAINST ANY COUNTRY!”
He warned of “economic warfare and isolation on an unprecedented scale” without giving details of any new sanctions planned.
Iran had urged Mr Trump to accept defeat, warning that the blockade on the strait would continue until the US president stops “indulging in fantasies” of an American victory. But Mr Trump remained defiant, saying on Wednesday that Iranian “maniacs” were “on the ropes”.
“Their navy is gone, their air force is destroyed, their military factories are now rubble, their currency is worthless, and their country is hanging by a thread,” he said.
Mr Trump claimed earlier this week that Hormuz could become a “new US territory” and on Wednesday he touted US military efforts to help ships travel the strait amid the threat of Iranian attacks.
Axios reported that US forces had quietly set up a shipping route through a southern channel of the strait along the coast of Oman, allowing 15 to 20 ships in and out each night in recent weeks.
The ships had carried millions of barrels of oil each day, “roughly half the pre-war volume”, two US officials told Axios.
“We have been controlling the southern lane of the Strait of Hormuz for two months now,” one source said.
“The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps can be a nuisance, but they don’t control the strait. We do.”
Iran: ‘Squeezing harder won’t win you concessions’
The Telegraph revealed last week that Mr Trump had settled on a stronger economic strategy after talks with Scott Bessent, the US treasury secretary.
The source said: “It’s been turned over to Bessent. Let him off the chain; he will destroy their currency.”
Aides reportedly pushed the strategy by showing Mr Trump statistics on how current sanctions were already crippling Iran.
US sanctions – called Operation Economic Fury – have choked Iran’s economy in recent months, driving the Iranian rial into free fall and accelerating triple-digit inflation. Red meat prices have tripled and fuel is rationed at the pumps.
They believe that increasing economic restrictions would “squeeze” the regime, forcing it to eventually make a deal to prevent total collapse.
Mr Bessent said last week that Iran would face “economic isolation, like the world has never seen before”.
Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf, Iran’s parliament speaker, said in response that the Americans erroneously thought “squeezing Iran harder” would win them concessions that were never part of the agreement to end the war.
In a post on X, he said Mr Bessent and Pete Hegseth, the US defence secretary, were “way out of their league” in trying to negotiate peace.
“Stop waiting for the clown crew to pull a rabbit out of their hat and clean up the mess you made,” Mr Qalibaf wrote.
summary: President Donald Trump announced what he termed an "economic D-Day" and the most crushing economic operation ever launched against Iran to pressure Tehran into accepting a deal to end the ongoing war. The financial warfare strategy, developed alongside US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, aims to isolate Iran economically and stop any lifeline support from other countries while talks and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz remain stalled. Meanwhile, US forces have quietly established a shipping route through a southern channel of the strait to allow millions of barrels of oil to pass daily. Iranian officials have dismissed the increased economic pressure, stating that squeezing Iran harder will not force them to make concessions.
key_points: Donald Trump declared an "economic D-Day" against Iran, threatening severe economic consequences for any countries providing lifelines to Tehran.
The new financial warfare strategy, developed with US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, follows stalled talks to end the US-Iran war and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.
US forces have quietly established a controlled shipping route along the coast of Oman to move millions of barrels of oil through the Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf rejected the increased economic pressure, stating that squeezing Iran harder will not win US concessions.

title: Lily Hooper: Missing teen hiker found dead in Australian bush after eight-day search
author: Tabby Wilson
content:
![A blonde woman in a green singlet is pictured in the left. On the right, the same woman is seen sitting on a plane, with her hair in two plaits.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/c439/live/7851db30-9c3b-11f1-853e-ad17ff71705c.jpg)
Lily Hooper, 18, was found dead after an eight-day search in the Australian bush
- Published
The body of a woman has been found in Australian bushland, following an eight-day search for a Sydney teenager reported missing last Wednesday.
Police said that while the body was yet to be formally identified, it was believed to be that of 18-year-old Lily Hooper. The confirmation came after the state premier told the New South Wales parliament that she had been found alive before later retracting the statement.
The teenager left her home in Sydney to go walking in a nearby national park on 12 August. Her family reported her missing later that night, after she failed to return home by 22:00.
Her car was found in a car park at the bottom of a challenging trail in the Nattai National Park.
Police said that the body was found in the Southern Highlands at approximately 11:30 local time on Thursday. Hooper's body had been found in dense vegetation and would likely have to be carried out on foot.
There was initial confusion as to Hooper's condition, after New South Wales Premier Chris Minns told a parliamentary hearing that she had been found alive. Local media suggested that her family had also been informed that she was alive.
Minns corrected himself shortly afterwards, and told the hearing that "Lily's body has been found" and she was deceased.
"This is obviously devastating, and I'm profoundly sad for her family and for all those concerned," said Minns, and apologised to the committee.
The New South Wales police commissioner Mal Lanyon told reporters that he "unreservedly" apologised for the "miscommunication".
In a press conference on Thursday afternoon, Assistant Police Commissioner Joseph Cassar did not directly respond to questions as to how Hooper's family came to be told she had been found alive.
He told reporters that there was a period of between eight to 10 minutes before the teenager's parents were given an updated report on her condition.
He said he did not know exactly what was said to the Hooper family, but that if he "could turn the clock back, I would certainly".
A multi-agency search for the missing bushwalker had taken place over the past week, with support from multiple NSW Police Force units including PolAir, the Rescue Unit, the Trail Bike Unit, the Mounted Unit and the Dog Unit.
Police have also been supported by the Rural Fire Service, the National Parks and Wildlife Service and almost 100 members of the Australian Defence Force.
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese paid tribute to the 18-year-old in parliament, calling Hooper's death an unspeakable tragedy.
"Lily Hooper had so much more to offer the world. Her passing, I have no doubt, will be felt very deeply," he said.
Opposition leader Angus Taylor, Hooper's local MP, said the initial incorrect reports that Hooper had been found alive made the family's loss even worse.
"We can only imagine what Lily's family is going through right now. Such news would be a nightmare for any parent, and we grieve for Lily's wider family," Taylor said.
summary: The body of 18-year-old Sydney teenager Lily Hooper was found in the Australian bush following an eight-day search that began after she failed to return from a walk in Nattai National Park. New South Wales Premier Chris Minns and police officials issued apologies after initially and incorrectly informing officials and family members that she had been found alive. A multi-agency search involving police, emergency services, and the Australian Defence Force had been underway since she was reported missing on August 12.
key_points: Lily Hooper, 18, went missing after leaving her Sydney home to walk in Nattai National Park on August 12.
Her body was found in dense vegetation in the Southern Highlands after an eight-day search.
The New South Wales premier and police officials apologized after mistakenly reporting that she was found alive.
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and local MP Angus Taylor paid tribute to Hooper and offered condolences to her family.

title: Tourists flee as smugglers drop dozens of migrants on Spanish beach
author: Graham Keeley
content:
Dozens of migrants stormed a beach in the south of Spain and caused tourists to flee on Wednesday.
More than 60 migrants jumped from a speedboat onto the beach, prompting tourists to pack up their things and leave. Some people on the beach were seen calling the police.
Before many of the migrants could even reach the beach, two men driving the vessel – a high-speed launch – turned it round and headed back out to the Mediterranean.
Migrants were seen leaping from the vessel into the water, before swimming ashore and walking past the sunbathers towards the nearby town of Atamaría in Murcia.
The incident happened at about 1pm on Wednesday at the secluded Cala del Barco near the La Manga resort in Murcia.
La Manga is known for its golf courses and football training facilities, which have been used by teams including the England national side and more recently Arsenal and Newcastle.
Francisco Bernabé, a conservative senator from the nearby town of La Unión, said in a social media post: “Dozens of illegal migrants today at La Manga cove.
“Why was it not possible to detect a vessel of those dimensions with all radars before? Are they broken? Do they have them turned off? Or are they working and they simply ignore them?”
‘This cannot be normalised’
Noelia Arroyo, the mayor of the nearby port city of Cartagena, told Cadena Ser radio: “This cannot be normalised.
“If a migrant can reach a cove like this, disembark in full view of citizens and leave, we have to ask ourselves how the control of our maritime borders is working?”
Spain’s civil guard later said they had arrested 45 men, two women and 15 boys. All were healthy, said the Red Cross. The migrants were handed over to Spain’s National Police, which deals with migration issues.
Most will be returned to their country of origin, but if they do claim asylum, they will undergo a lengthy process to evaluate their claims.
This is the latest incident of migrants being dropped off by traffickers on beaches after travelling at high speeds across the Mediterranean from Morocco or Algeria to Spain.
summary: Dozens of migrants arrived on a beach in southern Spain after being dropped off by traffickers on a high-speed vessel, causing tourists to flee. Spanish authorities subsequently arrested 45 men, two women, and 15 boys, all of whom were reported to be healthy. Local officials criticized the apparent lack of maritime border detection following the midday incident.
key_points: More than 60 migrants jumped from a speedboat onto Cala del Barco beach in Murcia on Wednesday.
The incident caused tourists to pack up and leave while some called the police.
Spain's civil guard arrested 45 men, two women, and 15 boys.
Local officials questioned the effectiveness of maritime border controls after the event.

title: ‘Republicans ran up the tab’: Democrats outraged over $40tn national debt – live
author: Vivian Ho; George Chidi; Andrew Lawrence; Michael Sainato
content:
Democrats and Republicans outraged over $40tn national debt
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of US politics.
The US gross national debt reached $40tn for the first time on Wednesday, the highest in US history.
The government deficit doubled over the past decade, with government spending growing under both Donald Trump and Joe Biden – Trump approved $8.4tn worth of debt during his first term, with a large chunk going to Covid-19 relief spending, while Biden approved $4.3tn worth of debt.
In fiscal year 2026, which began in October 2025, $1.8tn has been added to the debt so far.
Both Democrats and Republicans responded to the milestone with outrage, with Democrats placing the blame on Trump and a Republican-controlled Congress for the uptick in spending.
“The President said he’d pay off the debt in his first term. Well we all knew that was a lie. Instead he ran it up to $40 trillion while he and his family made billions,” Mark Kelly, a Democratic senator from Arizona, posted on X.
“Republicans ran up the tab, handed billionaires another tax break, and now wanna lecture working families about ‘fiscal responsibility’. You can’t max out the card AND pretend you’re the accountant. Pick a struggle,” Jasmine Crockett, a Democratic congresswoman from Texas, said.
“The Republican One Big Ugly Bill adds over $4 trillion alone—all to shamefully give tax breaks to billionaires and corporations,” Jason Crow, a Democratic congressman from Colorado, posted on X.
Crow is referring to the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which the non-partisan Congressional Budget Office estimates will increase the deficit by $3.3tn. After Republican senator Rick Scottposted on X that “Congress needs to get spending under control”, netizens were quick to add that he had voted to pass this bill.
Republican congressman Thomas Massie, who regularly clashed with Trump and his own party as well as with his colleagues across the aisle, has long worn on his suit jacket a debt badge, a three-inch-long pin he created that updates the national debt in real time. “When I invented the debt badge, the national debt was just over $31 trillion,” he posted on X.
“$4,000 per year per American. That’s how much interest we are paying on the debt to banks & foreign countries every year. A family of four owes $16,000 per year for nothing but interest on the debt!” Massie said. “I lost my re-election because I voted against the policies that caused this.” In May, the seven-term incumbent lost the House primary to keep his seat to Ed Gallrein, a retired Navy Seal and farmer who was recruited into the race by Trump.
Michele Tafoya: from unassuming NFL sideline reporter to rightwing firebrand
Andrew Lawrence
As the third leg of NBC’s Sunday Night Football crew alongside play-by-play man Al Michaels and the tart-tongued analyst Cris Collinsworth, Michele Tafoya was a paragon of deference and neutrality for 11 years as an NFL sideline reporter, dutifully relating boilerplate tactics, talking points and injury updates when she wasn’t nodding along to softball interviews or fumbling through hammy production gimmicks for viewers who might have been too offline to get the bit.
She was almost pathologically committed to not doing anything to draw attention to herself or her gender in an era when sideline reporting was a fast track to national celebrity. Even her football takes hewed to the middle. (“New Orleans doesn’t want to lose to Atlanta twice in a season …”) Anyone who says they saw the 61-year-old emerging as a rightwing firebrand was watching a different game.
And yet here we are. Last week, Tafoya was the decisive winner of Minnesota’s US Senate Republican primary, earning the party’s nomination for November’s general election. Even more striking: she beat back eight challengers, not least Adam Schwarze, the party-endorsed pro-gun, pro-military ex-Navy SEAL, and Royce White, the anti-leftist, anti-trans NBA flameout currently testing WNBA gender norms.
From McDonald’s to Congress: can a former fry cook flip a key district for Democrats?
Michael Sainato
During his presidential campaign in October 2024, Donald Trumpstaged a photo op at a McDonald’s franchise in Pennsylvania, where he was briefly taught how to work the fryer and drive-thru window at the closed restaurant, while making several unsubstantiated claims about Kamala Harris’s past summer job at McDonald’s.
The posturing around McDonald’s garnered significant publicity, as Trump and Republicans capitalized on an affordability crisis triggered by high inflation that occurred globally due to the Covid pandemic.
Now, as Trump’s promises to “end inflation” and bring down prices have fallen flat, a real former fry cook is hoping affordability will help him flip Colorado’s eighth congressional district, a swing district narrowly won by the Republican Gabe Evans in 2024. The district is rated a toss-up by the Cook Partisan Index, and affordability is front and center in Democratic nominee Manny Rutinel’s congressional campaign.
Iran foreign minister points to US national debt as Trump threatens 'economic warfare'
Donald Trump on Wednesday posted that he intends to inflict on Iran “the MOST CRUSHING ECONOMIC OPERATION EVER TAKEN AGAINST ANY COUNTRY!”
“This will be Economic Warfare and Isolation on an unprecedented scale,” the president said.
On Thursday, Abbas Araghchi, Iran’s minister of foreign affairs posted on X screenshots from various news outlets reporting that the US national debt had reached $40tnfor the first time in history.
“The so-called ‘Economic D-Day’ is a diversion from America’s own crisis: unprecedented debt and surging interest costs,” Araghchi said. “Doubling down on failed policies will only bring further defeat — and enmity of Iranians. US economic terrorism threatens global economy and sovereignty worldwide.”

Government spending and deficits have grown over the past decade under both Donald Trump and Joe Biden, with lawmakers placing blame across party lines. title: Telemundo executive among seven killed in tourist helicopter crash in Kenya
author: Nicholas Komu
content:
Seven people, including a US media executive and four other Americans, have died after a safari helicopter crashed in a remote region of northern Kenya on Wednesday.
The Kenya Civil Aviation Authority confirmed that an investigation is underway after the crash, which occurred at 9:13 a.m. while the aircraft was traveling from the Loisaba Conservancy to the Ewaso Nyiro region in Samburu County. Six passengers and a pilot were on board the flight.
David Nkoroi, the police commander for Samburu, told reporters that all seven people on the aircraft were killed.
NBCUniversal later said that José Alberto Suárez — president and general manager of Telemundo 31, Telemundo 49, and Telemundo Ft. Myers–Naples — was killed in the crash.
![Rescue officials at the site of the tourist helicopter crash](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/08/19/17/2026-08-19T123632Z_1187684725_RC2O1NAA1PEP_RTRMADP_3_KENYA-HELICOPTER-CRASH-TOURISM.JPG)
The 55-year-old, who had 25 years of experience in the media, was among five Americans who were killed in the crash.
“We are heartbroken to learn the tragic news that José was killed in a helicopter accident in Kenya,” NBCU Newsgroup Chairman Cesar Conde, NBCU Local Chairman Valari Staab and Telemundo Station Group President Jose Cancela wrote in a joint statement.
“José was an exceptional colleague who cared deeply about his teams, the communities they served and the important role our stations play in people’s lives. He brought energy, humor, warmth and a strong sense of purpose to his work, and his impact was felt far beyond the stations he led. Our hearts are with his loved ones, and with all of José’s colleagues and friends who are grieving this terrible loss.”
The other victims were identified by Kenyan police as Roger Edward Duarte; Adam Martin Hlavaty; Henry Parra; Stephany Maria Hollihan Vasconez; Michele Sensi Contugi; and pilot Josh Outram, ABC News reported.
Duarte was a fixture of Miami’s restaurant scene and the founder of George Stone Crab, according to the Miami New Times. “Roger was an angel,” a friend wrote. “My beloved friend since college. His wife, too. They embodied love, light, and loyalty.”
Parra and Hlavaty were a married South Florida couple who enjoyed traveling, NBC News reported.
Contugi, an Ecuadorian intelligence official, was married to Vasconez, who was a dual US citizen, according to The New York Post. Ecuador’s president expressed his condolences over the passing of Contugi and Vasconez in a Wednesday X post.
The US state department wrote, “The U.S. Embassy is in touch with local authorities and is providing consular assistance. We extend our deepest condolences to the families and loved ones on their loss.”
Local media reported that the aircraft went down in a rugged area near the base of Mount Ololokwe, a popular destination for visitors.
![Five Americans were killed in the wreck, including a US media executive](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/08/19/17/2026-08-19T162830Z_428945308_RC2R1NAYCHGD_RTRMADP_3_KENYA-HELICOPTER-CRASH-TOURISM.JPG)
The helicopter, owned by local firm Lady Lori Helicopters, was transporting guests associated with the travel operator &Beyond. In a statement, Lady Lori Helicopters noted that the aircraft was performing a charter flight when the crash occurred.
To assist with search and rescue operations, local safari operator Tropic Air Kenya stated that it dispatched two of its helicopters to the scene.
The civil aviation authority specified that the involved aircraft was a Eurocopter EC130 B4.
Emergency response teams from the Kenya Red Cross were “participating in a multiagency response effort as rescue teams work to access the crash site,” the organization said.
The incident comes amid a growing number of helicopter crashes in Kenya, where the tourism industry relies heavily on domestic aviation companies to transport travelers to distant landmarks like Mount Ololokwe.
In February, six people, including a legislator, were killed when a helicopter crashed in a hilly part of western Kenya.
summary: Seven people, including five Americans and a Telemundo executive, died when a safari helicopter crashed in a remote region of northern Kenya. The aircraft was traveling from the Loisaba Conservancy to the Ewaso Nyiro region when it went down near Mount Ololokwe. The Kenya Civil Aviation Authority has confirmed that an investigation into the crash is underway.
key_points: Seven people were killed, consisting of six passengers and the pilot.
Five of the victims were American citizens, including Telemundo executive José Alberto Suárez.
The aircraft was a Eurocopter EC130 B4 operated by Lady Lori Helicopters.
The crash occurred in a rugged area near Mount Ololokwe during a charter flight.

title: Natalie Harp stowed in trunk of SUV when Trump’s motorcade had no space: report
author: Owen Scott
content:
The estranged brother of Natalie Harp, Donald Trump’s doting aide, struggled to contain his laughter when told of the reported lengths his sister went to accompany Trump to a court hearing.
Preston Harp initially burst out laughing when CNN’s Erin Burnett asked for his reaction to the network’s report that his sister jumped into the trunk of an SUV when there wasn’t space for her to ride in Trump’s motorcade on the way to a court hearing in New York City in October 2023.
The network reports that a “screaming match” took place in the lobby of Trump Tower after there was no room for Natalie Harp in the motorcade. The aide reportedly insisted she had been asked by Trump to attend the hearing, but with no seat available, she climbed into the trunk of an SUV, according to sources and a photograph seen by CNN.
“That's really funny, I didn't know about that,” Preston Harp told CNN's Erin Burnett OutFront through laughter.
Burnett then asked him, “You're laughing, but I mean, is it funny or what? You know her, so that's why...”
![Preston Harp initially burst out laughing when CNN’s Erin Burnett asked for his reaction to the network’s report](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/08/19/14/22/preston-harp.png)
“No, it’s not, I'm sorry, it’s actually sad,” Preston Harp added. “That’s obsession. That’s like an unhealthy obsession with someone if you’re going to jump into the trunk of their car.”
Natalie Harp’s estranged sibling, a Trump critic, also detailed more about his upbringing with his sister, claiming that his mom believed in American exceptionalism.
“Trump is like everything that my mom taught us to respect,” he said. “I think that's where her infatuation with Trump comes from, honestly.”
The reported trunk incident is another example of Natalie Harp’s devotion to the president, which has “unnerved” some of her White House colleagues, according to The New York Times.
She has come under the spotlight this week, with multiple reports detailing how she became one of his most trusted supporters. The executive assistant is often seen by the president’s side, having cultivated a close working relationship since she first came to Trump’s attention in 2019.
She joined Trump’s staff in 2022, having claimed he “saved her life” after she was diagnosed with stage II bone cancer. She hit the headlines earlier this month when it emerged she was one of a small number of aides who were transferred to a military plane in Turkey to avoid a suspected assassination threat by Iran.
One unnamed White House advisor told CNN that Trump “likes the attention and the fact that she is 100 percent committed and loyal.”
“She doesn’t second-guess, doesn’t question,” the advisor said of Natalie Harp, who has also reportedly earned the nickname of “human printer” for handing the president hard copies of social media posts and newspaper articles.
Democratic senator Jon Ossoff drew further attention to Natalie Harp this week after suggesting at a rally Trump would rather fly with “Natalie on their apparently defenseless flying palace” than do his job.
The Trump administration has vociferously defended her, with the official Rapid Response 47 account on X tearing into a CNN correspondent who asked the president about the aide.
She was described as “one of the most loyal and hardest working aides on President Trump’s team” in a statement by White House spokesman Davis Ingle this week.
And Ossoff, meanwhile, was branded a “radical, extremist Dumocrat” by White House communications director Steven Cheung in a social media response to his speech.
summary: Donald Trump's aide Natalie Harp reportedly climbed into the trunk of an SUV during an October 2023 motorcade ride to a New York City court hearing after a dispute over a lack of seating. Her estranged brother, Preston Harp, reacted to the report by calling her actions an unhealthy obsession, while acknowledging her deep devotion to Trump. Harp is known for her absolute loyalty to Trump, having worked closely with him since joining his staff in 2022.
key_points: Natalie Harp reportedly rode in the trunk of an SUV during a New York City motorcade in October 2023 because there was no room for her inside.
Her estranged brother, Preston Harp, described the incident as an "unhealthy obsession" during an interview with CNN.
Harp is known for her extreme loyalty to Trump, earning the nickname "human printer" for providing him with hard copies of articles and social media posts.
The Trump administration has strongly defended Harp, describing her as one of the hardest-working and most loyal aides on the team.

title: Russia launches ‘massive attack’ on Kyiv and surrounding region – Europe live
author: Jakub Krupa; Dan Sabbagh
content:
At least 12 people were killed and 40 injured in a series of Russian attacks on the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv.
A boy looks at a damaged residential building following a Russian strike in Kyiv. Photograph: Tetiana Dzhafarova/AFP/Getty Images
“It was a massive attack – the Russians had been preparing for a long time, combining different types of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones, aiming to cause as much damage as possible to civilian infrastructure. There is destruction in Kyiv and the region, as well as in the Odesa and Chernihiv regions,” Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.
The attack will likely draw further attention to Ukraine’s shortage of air defence missiles.
“While Moscow is investing in ballistic missiles and escalation, such strikes do not always receive the response they should from the world. And as long as Ukraine does not have enough anti-ballistic defence, Russia will not consider peace seriously,” Zelenskyy warned this morning.
Pledging with allies to send more Patriot interceptors to help protect Ukraine, he stressed that “every additional missile saves the lives of our people.”
More drone attack warnings from Kyiv were going live this morning.
Responding to the overnight attacks, Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko declared Friday a day of mourning in the city.
I will bring you more updates throughout the day.
It’s Thursday, 20 August 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.
Russia testing Nato's resolve with airspace incidents in neighbouring countries, Ukraine's minister warns
Ukraine’s foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said that Russia violated the airspace of Moldova and Romania during last night’s attacks on Ukraine.
“These are not isolated incidents. They are part of Russia’s deliberate and systemic terrorist attacks. The aggressor state is increasingly testing the resolve of Nato and its partners, violating the sovereignty of neighbouring states and deliberately expanding the risks posed by its war far beyond Ukraine,” he warned.
Sybiha said he would work with his counterparts in both countries “toward a stronger and more effective regional response to Russia’s cynical attempts to widen the war it started.”
“Our collective response must be stronger than Russia’s attempts to test our unity and resolve. The security and stability of the entire region are at stake,” he said.
A children’s hospital was struck in the Solomianskyi district to the west of the heart of the capital, with windows blown out and cars burned. At least two residential buildings were also reported hit in the area.
Residents walk through debris in a courtyard following a Russian missile strike on Kyiv. Photograph: Diego Fedele/Getty Images
Explosions could be heard from the city centre at about midnight on Wednesday, earlier than the normal timing of Russian missile strikes, and there was a further wave of attacks early on Thursday morning.
An attack in Brovary district of the broader Kyiv region killed one man and wounded another, said the regional governor, Tymur Tkachenko. “One industrial facility has been damaged. All relevant services are on site, working to extinguish the fire,” he said.
Ukraine’s air force had warned of Russian Kalibr cruise missiles passing over the regional village of Kaharlyk and heading towards the capital.
Russia-controlled Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant loses external power supply
The United Nations nuclear watchdog said on Thursday that Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power station lost its only remaining external power line, forcing emergency diesel generators to start supplying vital safety systems, Reuters reported.
The International Atomic Energy Agency, or IAEA, said on X that initial assessment indicated the damage was located on the northern bank of the Dnipro River, and technicians were unable to determine the outage’s cause due to military activity.
The plant, Europe’s largest with six reactors, produces no electricity but needs power supplied by two external links to keep nuclear fuel cool, Reuters said.
Ukraine’s air force said that Russia had launched dozens of ballistic, cruise, and hypersonic missiles, as well as 168 drones in its overnight attack on the country.
It said that air defence units downed 145 drones and most of the cruise missiles but none of the missiles that run on ballistic trajectory, Reuters said.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has for month been pushing for more anti-ballistic missiles to be delivered to Ukraine.
18 people hospitalised after overnight attacks on Kyiv
Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko said 18 people have been hospitalised after the overnight attacks, with emergency and clean-up response continuing at various sites across three districts of the city.
“The capital is recovering from a massive enemy attack,” he said in a video on Telegram.
“Residential and non-residential buildings, a school, and a children’s hospital were damaged,” he added.

There is destruction in Kyiv and the region, as well as in the Odesa and Chernihiv regions,” Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.
The attack will likely draw further attention to Ukraine’s shortage of air defence missiles.
“While Moscow is investing in ballistic missiles and escalation, such strikes do not always receive the response they should from the world. And as long as Ukraine does not have enough anti-ballistic defence, Russia will not consider peace seriously,” Zelenskyy warned this morning.
Pledging with allies to send more Patriot interceptors to help protect Ukraine, he stressed that “every additional missile saves the lives of our people.”
More drone attack warnings from Kyiv were going live this morning.
Responding to the overnight attacks, Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko declared Friday a day of mourning in the city.

It’s Thursday, 20 August 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.
summary: Russia launched a massive overnight attack utilizing ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones against Kyiv and surrounding regions, resulting in at least 12 deaths and 40 injuries. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy highlighted Ukraine's severe shortage of anti-ballistic defense systems and called on allies for more Patriot interceptors. Additionally, officials reported that Russian strikes violated the airspace of Moldova and Romania, and caused the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant to lose its external power supply.
key_points: At least 12 people were killed and 40 injured in coordinated Russian missile and drone strikes across Kyiv and other regions.
President Zelenskyy urged international allies to supply more anti-ballistic defense missiles, noting that none of the incoming ballistic missiles were intercepted.
Ukraine's foreign minister stated that Russian drones and missiles violated the airspace of neighboring Moldova and Romania.
The Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant lost its last remaining external power line, forcing the activation of emergency diesel generators.
Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko declared Friday a day of mourning following the widespread damage to residential buildings, schools, and a children's hospital.

title: Erin Patterson appeal: Mushroom killer must stay in jail forever for 'truly dreadful' crime, prosecutors say
author: Katy Watson; Simon Atkinson
content:
![A courtroom sketch shows Erin Patterson attending proceedings via a video link from the Dame Phyllis Frost Centre, in the Victorian Court of Appeal in Melbourne, Australia, August 19](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/999/cpsprodpb/5ba2/live/bbb890d0-9c5e-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
Erin Patterson attended the Court of Appeal via video link from prison
- Published
An Australian court has been told that the crimes of mushroom murderer Erin Patterson were "truly dreadful" and that she should never be allowed to leave prison.
Crown prosecutors are appealing against a sentence they call "manifestly inadequate" as it allows for the possibility of parole.
Patterson was jailed for life after killing three of her relatives and trying to kill another by serving them a beef Wellington containing death cap mushrooms at her Victoria home in 2023.
The 51-year-old, who attended the Court of Appeal via video link from prison, will be eligible to be freed after 33 years.
The Court of Appeal in Melbourne has also heard a challenge from Patterson's lawyers as they try to overturn her convictions.
The judges say they will reserve their decisions, meaning it will likely be weeks or months before the outcome of both appeals is known.
Patterson's victims include her in-laws Don and Gail Patterson, both 70, and Gail's sister Heather Wilkinson, 66, who all died after what prosecutors called "shocking illnesses" as a result of the poisoning.
The only surviving guest, Heather's husband Ian Wilkinson, has never fully recovered from his ordeal, they said.
![Erin Patterson looks at the camera from the back of a police van](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/a44a/live/9cbc7300-9c62-11f1-827b-69a6492daae1.jpg)
Patterson will be eligible to be freed after 33 years
Outlining why Patterson's crime was so "dreadful", they talked of the "betrayal of trust" of family members whom she had invited for lunch.
It was, they said, the culmination of a plan she had "orchestrated " for months, including finding and preparing enough death caps to kill and "concocting a fantastic lie" to explain the lunch.
"The lunch guests had been good to the respondent and her children over many years," prosecutors said. "Not only did the respondent sit by and watch her victims consume the deadly meal over chit-chat and banter, but the meal ended with a prayer for her, following her lie about having been diagnosed with cancer. "
As the guests lay critically ill, Patterson did not admit to using foraged mushrooms, choosing instead to lie to police and health workers.
"Even when she knew that some of the victims were on life support, she maintained her lies," the prosecutors said,
At sentencing in September last year, Justice Christopher Beale said he was giving Patterson a glimmer of hope of release, solely because of her "harsh" prison conditions, telling her "there is a substantial chance that, for your protection, you will continue to be held in solitary confinement for years to come".
But the prosecutors say this was "overstated", arguing her conditions would improve over time, especially as her notoriety faded.
In court, prosecutor Brendan Kissane listed the activities open to Patterson in prison, including an exercise yard and access to hobbies including crocheting. According to reporters in court, at this point, the triple murderer closed her eyes and shook her head.
While prosecutors say Patterson should never be freed, they argue that if the appeal court disagreed, then it should at least increase the minimum sentence â calling 33 years "manifestly inadequate".
The minimum term open to the judge for the offences was 30 years. In written arguments, they said an additional three years "utterly fails to reflect the gravity of the offending or vindicate the dignity of each of the four victims".
Arguing for the punishment to be left as it was Patterson's lawyers said the judge's reasoning had been "impeccable" and had "clearly taken into account all relevant considerations" and "made appropriate findings about how serious this matter was".
Earlier on Thursday prosecutors wrapped up their challenges to Patterson's appeal to have her convictions thrown out.
Patterson's lawyers had argued last year's trial was undermined by a "catastrophic" mix-up that led to the jury staying at the same hotel as prosecutors and a key witness, and that some evidence in the trial was too speculative to have been put before the jury and caused a miscarriage of justice.
- ![Erin Patterson during trial in Melbourne wearing glasses and her dark her down.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1248/cpsprodpb/0306/live/58d0af30-9adc-11f1-b792-a710e56a11dc.jpg)
  - Published12 July 2025
 ![A designed image of Erin Patterson beside mushrooms](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/58cb/live/946cda10-5e7d-11f0-a40e-a1af2950b220.png)
summary: Crown prosecutors in Australia are appealing the life sentence of Erin Patterson, arguing she should never be released and calling her current 33-year minimum term manifestly inadequate. Patterson was convicted of killing three relatives and attempting to kill a fourth by serving them a beef Wellington containing death cap mushrooms in 2023. Meanwhile, Patterson's lawyers are simultaneously challenging her convictions in the Court of Appeal, with judges reserving their decisions for a later date.
key_points: Erin Patterson was jailed for life for killing three relatives and trying to kill a fourth using death cap mushrooms in 2023.
Prosecutors argued that Patterson's crimes were a dreadful betrayal of trust that warrant keeping her in prison forever without the possibility of parole.
Patterson's legal team is challenging her convictions, citing a hotel mix-up involving the jury and allegedly speculative evidence.
Judges have reserved their decisions on both the sentence appeal and the conviction challenge, with outcomes expected in weeks or months.

title: Trump threatens Iran’s trade partners, as military strikes make way for economic pressure
author: Jonathan Yerushalmy
content:
Donald Trump has announced a new campaign to isolate Iran’s economy, threatening “tremendous economic consequences” on any country that helps or does business with Tehran, a move that could set up a fresh confrontation with China if implemented.
“Today, I am announcing the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country!” Trump wrote on Truth Social. “Any country that allows its financial institutions, businesses, airports, or government entities to provide any type of lifeline to Iran will itself face tremendous economic consequences.”
His announcement however contained no detail on what actions would be taken or which countries could be affected, and comes as the war nears its six-month mark, with the president facing pressure over the cost of the conflict as the US midterm elections approach.
Last month the US president paused attacks on Iran, after a fortnight of nightly strikes that had failed to bring officials in Tehran back to the negotiating table and reports that the war has run down US stockpiles of key munitions. Pentagon advisers reportedly told Trump last month that the US had nearly exhausted its list of targets in Iran and the military campaign had reached the limits of its effectiveness.
The White House has signalled in recent weeks a shift in strategy to tightening pressure on Iran economically. US treasury secretary Scott Bessent said last week the US would begin ramping up efforts to isolating Iran economically.
The US treasury has for months been carrying out an effort, called Operation Economic Fury, aiming to cut off Iran’s funding with targeted sanctions, while a naval blockade in the straight of Hormuz has sought to block Iranian ports from exporting oil vital to keeping the country’s economy afloat.
Iran’s economy already faces a punishing array of US and western sanctions that have ground down the economy over years and curtailed its ability to sell oil. But experts say the country’s leaders have learned to adapt to the measures, including by exporting oil through a sophisticated network of shadow tankers.
In his announcement on Wednesday, Trump listed several activities that he said needed to stop immediately, including “oil smuggling, swap lines, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries, front companies”.
The wording of the president’s announcement suggested that he could be threatening secondary sanctions on country’s that buy Iranian oil, but experts say such a move could lead to direct confrontation with China – Iran’s biggest trading partner – at a time when the US is trying to establish a new trading relationship with Beijing.
“Whatever new economic measures the US can use will need to be directed at Iran’s trading partners,” said Gregory Brew, a senior analyst at theEurasia Group, adding that it will be “hard for the US to direct such actions at China, the country that matters most to Iran’s economic future.”
Chinese leader Xi Jinping is also expected to visit the US next month, further complicating any efforts to target Beijing’s imports of Iranian oil.
Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Iran’s supreme leader, said on Tuesday that military pressure and sanctions would not break Iran’s resolve. He added that Iran remained open to dialogue with the US, but would not confuse negotiations with surrender, according to the semi-official Fars news agency.
On Tuesday, the United Arab Emirates, announced it would suspend all trade activities, commercial exchanges and financial transactions with Iran, after it said it had detected two missiles launched from the country. Tehran dismissed the reports as baseless.
Prior to the war, the UAE was one of Iran’s biggest trade partners, providing more than 30% of its imports.
Earlier on Wednesday, Trump also claimed that vessels from Gulf countries allied with the US were continuing to move through the strait of Hormuz, despite the Iranian threat to shipping in the waterway. The president said the US military was aiding ships in the strait, saying “right now, a lot of boats are coming through.”
Axios reported that US forces were facilitating the transit of 15 to 20 ships in and out of the Hormuz each night in recent weeks – carrying “roughly half the prewar volume” of daily oil shipments – while also continuing to blockade Iranian exports. Those volumes were disputed by some, with ship tracking data from Kpler showing transits remained low.
Referring to the Axios report, Danny Citrinowicz, the former head of the Iran branch of Israeli military intelligence, said it was an important operational development, but questioned how long the US government would be able to sustain such an operation.
“More importantly, this will not force Iran to surrender or fundamentally change its negotiating position,” said Citrinowicz.
summary: Donald Trump has announced a new campaign of economic pressure against Iran, threatening severe consequences for any country or business that trades with Tehran. This shift from military strikes to economic isolation follows months of conflict and dwindling US munitions, though it lacks specific details on implementation. The move could potentially spark a confrontation with China, Iran's largest trading partner, while the United Arab Emirates recently announced a suspension of all trade with Iran.
key_points: Trump announced a new economic isolation campaign against Iran, threatening severe consequences for its trade partners.
The strategy shift follows a pause in US military strikes after Pentagon advisers reported the campaign had reached its limits.
Targeting Iran's trade partners could lead to a confrontation with China, Iran's biggest trading partner, ahead of an expected visit by Xi Jinping.
The United Arab Emirates recently announced the suspension of all trade and financial transactions with Iran following missile launch allegations.
Iran's leadership stated that sanctions and military pressure will not break the country's resolve.

title: Russia unleashes 'massive attack' on Kyiv, killing at least eight
author: Harry Sekulich
content:
![Firefighters work at a site hit by a Russian missile strike, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in Kyiv on 20 August.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/6d90/live/3ec0fe10-9c53-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
Firefighters battle a blaze at warehouse in Kyiv in the early hours of Thursday
- Published
A wave of overnight Russian missile strikes has killed at least eight people in the capital Kyiv and the surrounding region, Ukrainian authorities say.
Apartment blocks and warehouses were hit in the "massive attack" on Thursday, according to the State Emergency Service of Ukraine (DSNS), while a children's hospital and school were damaged. At least 33 people were injured.
Authorities are working to rescue people trapped underneath the rubble of demolished buildings, with crews already pulling two survivors from debris.
Meanwhile, Romania said one drone crossed into its territory at the northern border with Ukraine triggering an air alert siren.
In the early hours of Thursday, "a drone entered Romanian national airspace, approximately 13 kilometres east of the city of GalaÈi," the Romanian defence ministry wrote in a statement.
The drone crashed into "an uninhabited area", causing a small fire that was extinguished.
"No casualties or material damage were reported", the ministry added, noting that the initial alert had been lifted.
The Polish military also said it had begun "defensive air operations" to protect its airspace, with the country sharing part of its south-eastern border with Ukraine.
![People take shelter inside an underground parking during Russian missile and drone strikes, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in Kyiv, Ukraine August 20, 2026](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/65d0/live/a826fe40-9c3a-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
Kyiv resident took shelter underground as sirens blared across the capital
Kyiv Mayor Vitaly Klitschko said a children's hospital had been damaged in the overnight strikes, where windows were broken and cars set ablaze nearby. There was also damage at an educational institution, he said.
An industrial centre in the Solomyanskyi district, south-west Kyiv, was also hit by missiles, according to the mayor.
An attack in Brovary district of the broader Kyiv region killed one man and wounded another, Kyiv regional governor Tymur Tkachenko said.
The regional administration issued an alert earlier in the night warning residents to take shelter. It continued: "Air defense operations are possible in the area".
More missile alerts were issued from regional authorities throughout the night, citing warnings from the Ukrainian air force that missiles were flying towards the capital.
The Russian airstrikes cut power to thousands of properties overnight, plunging parts of the Kyiv region into darkness, with technicians racing to repair the damaged energy grids.
The Russian defence ministry claims to have targeted a drone component production facility and a munition depot in Kyiv, according to state-run media, although the claims have not been independently verified by the BBC.
![A resident stands at a site of an apartment building hit by a Russian missile strike, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in Kyiv, Ukraine August 20.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/6b81/live/573bbf90-9c56-11f1-a9a9-5b357edb8f56.jpg)
Cars erupt in flames during overnight strikes in Kyiv
Kyiv has been battered in near nightly-attacks in recent weeks, with some strikes resulting in dozens of deaths and serious injuries.
More than a dozen regions have been targeted across Ukraine over the past week, President Volodymyr Zelensky said, with Russia launching more than 1,550 attack drones, 1,560 guide aerial bombs and 62 missiles Ukraine.
Ukraine has stepped up its attacks deep inside Russia during the past few weeks, with a recent flurry of 600 drones targeting Moscow.
Two separate attacks on Russia this week has killed at least 16 people, including one child.
Since July, Ukraine has repeatedly targeted a warehouse belonging to the online retailer Wildberries, known as Russia's version of Amazon. Ukraine's defence ministry said the latest attack meant that seven out of 10 of the largest Wildberries logistics centres had been "disabled".
While the attacks on Russia are partly intended to increase pressure on Moscow to engage in peace talks to end the four and a half year war, there has been little movement on diplomatic efforts to broker a ceasefire deal.
Both sides accuse each other of targeting civilians.
Russia first launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and currently controls about one-fifth of Ukrainian territory â largely concentrated in the eastern border regions.
summary: A massive overnight wave of Russian missile and drone strikes on Kyiv and the surrounding region killed at least eight people and injured 33 others. The attacks damaged apartment blocks, warehouses, a children's hospital, and a school, while cutting power to thousands of properties. Additionally, neighboring Romania reported that a drone crossed into its territory and crashed in an uninhabited area, prompting the Polish military to begin defensive air operations.
key_points: Overnight Russian missile strikes killed at least eight people and injured 33 in Kyiv and the surrounding region.
Apartment buildings, warehouses, a school, and a children's hospital were damaged in the attack.
A drone crossed from Ukraine into Romanian airspace and crashed in an uninhabited area without causing casualties.
The Polish military initiated defensive air operations to protect its airspace.
The Russian defense ministry claimed to have targeted a drone component production facility and a munition depot.

title: Trump threatens 'tremendous economic consequences' on any country helping Iran
author: Grace Eliza Goodwin; Peter Hoskins
content:
![Trump, wearing a suit and no tie and a white "USA" hat, descending from airplane steps](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/725b/live/5ef21940-9c2a-11f1-aa8e-d328e95deb46.jpg)
- Published
President Donald Trump has said the US will inflict "TREMENDOUS Economic Consequences" on any country that helps or does business with Iran.
He wrote in all capital letters on Truth Social that he was launching "the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country!" He gave no further details, and did not name any other nation.
It comes after a 60-day ceasefire with Iran expired on Monday, with no sign of a diplomatic or military off-ramp to the conflict that the US and Israel began at the end of February.
Trump's latest move appears to extend the pressure campaign of Operation Economic Fury, launched in April to sanction foreign banks or firms that do business with Tehran.
In Wednesday evening's social media post, Trump said he was launching "economic D-Day" on Iran because the Islamic Republic had failed to make a deal with the US.
"ANY country that allows its financial institutions, businesses, airports, or government entities to provide any type of lifeline to Iran will itself face TREMENDOUS Economic Consequences," Trump said.
He did not specify what punishment countries might face.
Trump continued: "Oil smuggling, swap lines, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries, front companies - It all needs to stop NOW. You know who you are."
It comes a day after the United Arab Emirates, a US ally, announced it would be severing all financial and economic ties with Iran, following a new missile threat from the country.
The UAE's defence ministry said it had detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iran targeting maritime traffic, both of which landed in the sea.
Iranian entities have long used Dubai's financial system to transfer money through exchange houses and shell companies.
Following the UAE's decision, Iran's armed forces warned neighbouring Gulf countries against providing support to the US military, saying any assistance given to US forces would be considered collusion.
While China was not named in the post, businesses there are the biggest buyers of oil from Iran, a key source of Tehran's funding.
Since the start of the war, Washington has sanctioned several so-called teapot refineries - privately owned oil processing plants, mostly based in Shandong province, eastern China.
At the time, China's Ministry of Commerce said the sanctions were "in violation of international law and the basic norms governing international relations".
It also issued an order stipulating that the sanctions "shall not be recognised, enforced, or complied with".
The BBC has contacted the Chinese embassy in Washington for comment in response to Trump's latest post.
Last week, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the US would soon impose economic isolation on Iran "like the world has never seen before".
In April, the US treasury department and the Pentagon announced Operation Economic Fury.
It aimed to dismantle Iran's revenue streams through sanctions and by stopping foreign international entities doing business with Iran. It also included a naval blockade to stop exports from the Islamic Republic.
The BBC has asked the White House and US treasury department for comment.
Earlier this week, Trump also reportedly threatened to bomb Oman - a US ally - if it "gets in the way" of his administration's own talks with Iran, during a phone interview with a Fox News reporter.
The US and Oman have been negotiating separately with Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a waterway that is vital to the global economy.
The conflict has significantly disrupted traffic through the key Strait of Hormuz shipping route, pushing up global energy prices.
Around 20% of the world's crude oil and liquified natural gas (LNG) usually passes through the strait.
Ahead of the US midterm elections in November, Trump faces pressure over how much the war is costing American consumers.
summary: President Donald Trump announced on social media that the United States will impose severe economic consequences on any country that conducts business with or assists Iran. This warning follows the expiration of a 60-day ceasefire and builds upon the pressure campaign known as Operation Economic Fury. Trump's declaration comes shortly after the UAE severed its financial ties with Iran and amid ongoing tensions involving oil smuggling, sanctions, and regional security.
key_points: President Trump threatened tremendous economic consequences for any nation helping or doing business with Iran.
The announcement follows the expiration of a 60-day ceasefire between the US, Israel, and Iran with no diplomatic off-ramp.
The United Arab Emirates recently announced it was severing all financial and economic ties with Iran following a missile threat.
China is a major buyer of Iranian oil and has previously rejected US sanctions targeting its refineries.
The ongoing conflict has significantly disrupted traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, increasing global energy prices.

title: Seven people, mostly foreign tourists, killed in helicopter crash in Kenya
author: AFP; The Associated Press
content:
![Rescue officials work at the site of a tourist helicopter crash that caused multiple casualties, according to the police, in Samburu County, Kenya, August 19, 2026. Kenya Red Cross/Handout via REUTERS THIS IMAGE HAS BEEN SUPPLIED BY A THIRD PARTY. NO RESALES. NO ARCHIVES. MANDATORY CREDIT.](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/reuters_6a85fcb2-1787165874.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
A helicopter taking tourists on a safari has crashed in a remote part of northern Kenya, killing all seven people on board, including an Ecuadorian official and an American journalist.
The helicopter crashed at 9:13am local time (06:13 GMT) on Wednesday while flying from the Loisaba Conservancy to the Ewaso Nyiro area in Samburu County, according to the Kenya Civil Aviation Authority, which said in a statement that an investigation was under way.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3Eleven killed in Kenya plane crash near Maasai Mara National Reserve
- list 2 of 3Medical plane crash in Kenya kills at least six, injures two
- list 3 of 3Bus carrying mourners overturns in Kenya, killing 25 people
Helicopter crashes have happened with increasing regularity in Kenya, which has a vibrant tourism industry that depends on domestic carriers to ferry visitors to distant places like Mount Ololokwe.
Six passengers and the pilot were on board the helicopter, officials said. David Nkoroi, the police commander for Samburu, told reporters that all seven people had died but did not reveal their identities.
Later on Wednesday, Ecuador’s Transport Minister Roberto Luque said the country’s intelligence chief Michele Sensi-Contugi and his wife, Stephany Hollihan, were among those killed in the crash.
